papers.title: Semiclassical state on algebra of observables for de Sitter space and time reversal symmetry
papers.abstract: In de Sitter static patch holography, coupling bulk quantum fields to an observer's dynamical clock yields a type II$_1$ von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}_+$ of gauge-invariant observables. However, the unique tracial state on this algebra fails to reproduce semiclassical bulk correlation functions. We resolve this issue by introducing a family of heavy-clock states, representing an observer reference frame with heavy inertia. We prove that in the heavy-clock limit, $n$-point correlation functions of gauge-invariant dressed observables reproduce the bulk quantum field correlation functions on de Sitter spacetime. Furthermore, we investigate a generalized observer Hamiltonian $\widehat{H}_{\rm obs}=|\widehat{\pi}|$ that incorporates both forward-running ($\pi\geq 0$) and backward-running ($\pi <0$) clocks. The resulting von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ of gauge-invariant observables remains a type~II$_1$ factor and is isomorphic to $\mathcal{M}_+\otimes M_2(\mathbb{C})$, where $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ is the algebra of $2\times2$ complex matrices transforming between the two clock orientations. Time-reversal symmetry is implemented in this setting as an anti-unitary operator that exchanges the two clock orientations, yielding a type~II$_1$ von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{F}$ of gauge-invariant, time-reversal-invariant observables. We generalize the heavy-clock state construction to both $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{F}$, showing that $n$-point correlation functions calculated in heavy-clock states match the corresponding semiclassical bulk correlation functions. Finally, by coupling Einstein gravity to the Brown--Kucha\v{r} dust field, we derive the observer Hamiltonian $\widehat{H}_{\rm obs}=|\widehat{\pi}|$ from a perturbative reduction along the observer's worldline in the $G \to 0$ limit. This provides a field-theoretic foundation for the observer model developed in this work.
papers.summary: The paper constructs heavy‑clock states in de Sitter static‑patch holography that reproduce semiclassical bulk correlators and extends the framework to include time‑reversal symmetry via a doubled clock orientation, yielding a type II₁ algebra of gauge‑invariant observables. It also derives the observer Hamiltonian from Einstein gravity coupled to Brown–Kuchař dust, providing a field‑theoretic justification for the heavy‑clock model.

papers.title: Defect conformal field theories with free-in-the-bulk fermions
papers.abstract: We study codimension-two conformal defects for massless fermions that are free in a four-dimensional bulk, but interact on a two-dimensional defect. The bulk Dirac equation strongly constrains defect conformal field theory data: it fixes the dimensions of operators in the bulk-defect operator product expansion and, for bulk-defect-defect three-point functions, enforces a double-twist relation when only one member of a shadow pair is allowed by unitarity. The lowest modes of monodromy defects provide an important exception, since both shadow partners can be unitary and their three-point functions are instead related by a shadow transform.   We illustrate these structures with defect interactions, including an exactly tractable bilinear flow and Gross-Neveu-type quartic couplings. At a perturbative mixed fixed point, we find an explicit interacting example in which the double-twist condition is violated and the two shadow channels combine to give a regular bulk-defect-defect correlation function.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes codimension‑two defects for free bulk fermions, showing that the bulk Dirac equation fixes bulk‑defect OPE data and imposes a double‑twist relation for defect three‑point functions, except for monodromy defects where both shadow partners are unitary. It further explores exactly solvable bilinear flows and Gross‑Neveu quartic couplings, finding a mixed fixed point where the double‑twist condition is violated and the two shadow channels combine into a regular bulk‑defect‑defect correlator.

papers.title: The dimensional reduction of the spin-3 and spin-4 partially broken Fronsdal models
papers.authors: D. Dalmazi, A. L. R. dos Santos
papers.abstract: Here we perform a Kaluza-Klein dimensional reduction from $D+1$ to $D$ dimensions of a partially broken Fronsdal model for spin-3 and spin-4. The reduced models describe massive spin-3 and spin-4 particles without extra propagating modes. They differ from Singh-Hagen models by quadratic terms which vanish on shell, similarly to their higher dimensional massless parents. A covariant description of the reduced models in terms of gauge invariant field combinations naturally leads to higher derivative models, contrary to lower spin cases ($s\le 2$).   For both $s=3$ and $s=4$ we have a rather peculiar massless limit. Although their particle content corresponds to the $\pm j$ helicities with $j=0,1, \cdots s$, as expected, they appear intertwined in a non trivial way preventing diagonalization through any local field redefinition.
papers.summary: This paper performs a Kaluza-Klein reduction of partially broken Fronsdal models for spin-3 and spin-4, yielding massive higher-spin actions in D dimensions that avoid extra propagating modes. The resulting theories exhibit non-trivial massless limits and higher-derivative structures, offering new insights for higher-spin dynamics that could inform holographic duals and higher-point amplitude analyses.

papers.title: Three-dimensional vacua of $G_2$ flux compactifications
papers.authors: Aravind Aikot, Julian Choi, Timm Wrase
papers.abstract: We study supersymmetric vacua of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ effective theories from type IIA, type IIB/type I, and heterotic compactifications on $G_2$-structure spaces. Superpotential homogeneity and the physical scalar metric yield universal vacuum relations and axion stabilization constraints without specifying the full moduli-space metric. We express AdS$_3$ scalar masses through $\Delta$, the scaling dimension of the corresponding operator in the dual two-dimensional conformal field theory. In massive type IIA AdS$_3$ vacua, we derive the bound $\Delta_{\max}\geq(20+4\sqrt{67})/7\approx 7.5$ and an exact dimension $\Delta_b=6$ for $B_2$ axions on the torsion-free branch. Type IIB type I and heterotic AdS$_3$ vacua contain a universal volume-dilaton mode with $\Delta_{\phi s}=4$. On the singlet-torsion type IIB branch, we also obtain the volume-dilaton mode with $\Delta_{\phi s}=20/7$ and $\Delta_b=16/7$. Every supersymmetric Minkowski vacuum in the retained classical closed-string theories possesses an exact volume-dilaton flat direction. We characterize physical large-flux limits after tadpole constraints and axionic identifications, and identify torsion obstructions to isotropic scale separation.
papers.summary: The paper classifies supersymmetric AdS$_3$ vacua from $G_2$ flux compactifications in type IIA, IIB, and heterotic settings, deriving universal relations for scalar masses in terms of dual CFT operator dimensions. It identifies bounds on scaling dimensions, exact values for axion modes, and shows that all classical Minkowski vacua possess a flat volume-dilaton direction, providing new data for AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ holography.

papers.title: One-loop QED effective action at finite temperature and density beyond HTL limit
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for computing the nonlocal one-loop effective action in scalar and spinor QED at finite temperature and chemical potential in arbitrary even spacetime dimensions. Based on the heat kernel expansion to quadratic order in background fields, the framework reduces the effective action form factors to a common fundamental kernel. By resumming the external-momentum expansion, we obtain explicit closed-form expressions for the massless form factors in terms of polylogarithms and their derivatives with respect to the order. The same method determines the coefficients of the small-mass expansion to arbitrary order. The resulting expressions retain the full dependence on external Euclidean momentum, temperature, and chemical potential, without invoking the soft-momentum approximation. We also derive the corresponding photon polarization operators and evaluate their static limits, obtaining the Debye screening masses and electromagnetic susceptibilities.
papers.summary: The authors compute the one-loop effective action for scalar and spinor QED at finite temperature and chemical potential in arbitrary even dimensions, using a heat kernel expansion to quadratic order and resumming momentum expansions to obtain closed-form form factors in terms of polylogarithms. They also derive photon polarization operators and static limits, yielding Debye masses and electromagnetic susceptibilities without the soft-momentum approximation.

papers.title: Characteristic Modes of Non-minimally Coupled Thick Branes
papers.authors: Jing-Xin Gong, Heng Guo, Yong-Tao Lu, Xin-Yi Pan
papers.abstract: Characteristic modes provide important information about the intrinsic properties and dynamical response of gravitational systems. In this work, we investigate characteristic modes of thick branes with a non-minimally coupled bulk scalar field. Two representative thick brane solutions are considered, corresponding to a single-kink scalar configuration and a deformed kink configuration with internal structure, respectively. By analyzing the tensor perturbation equations, we first examine the localization of the graviton zero mode in the two brane models. For both brane models, the graviton zero mode is localized on the brane. No pronounced resonant Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes are found for the single-kink brane at $\xi=1/7$. For the deformed brane, we investigate the resonant KK modes at $\xi=0.99$, finding that increasing the deformation parameter $k$ leads to more resonant modes and a longer-lived first resonance.   We then calculate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of both brane models independently in the frequency and time domains. The quasinormal frequencies (QNFs) obtained by the independent methods agree well for the low overtones. The masses and decay rates of the resonant KK modes agree closely with the real parts and the magnitudes of the imaginary parts of the corresponding QNFs, respectively.
papers.summary: The paper studies tensor perturbations of two non‑minimally coupled thick brane solutions, showing that the graviton zero mode is localized and that resonant Kaluza–Klein modes appear only in the deformed brane. Quasinormal mode analysis confirms the masses and decay rates of these resonances, matching the real and imaginary parts of the QNFs.

papers.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
papers.abstract: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $\gamma=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.
papers.summary: The authors construct a new chiral algebra of central charge eight inside the lattice VOA (V_{E_6oplus A_2}), generated by two commuting (mathfrak{sl}_2) current algebras at levels 1 and 39 and a weight‑two field. They conjecture this algebra is strongly rational and its representation category equals the Drinfeld center of the Haagerup fusion category, leading to a holomorphic (E_8) extension with topological defect symmetry.

papers.title: PINNs for N=2* holography
papers.abstract: Can a holographic theory be reconstructed from its equation of state? We investigate this question using physics-informed neural networks in the bosonic-mass sector of the Pilch--Warner model. We first validate the PINN approach against an analytic solution encoding the leading high-temperature corrections to the conformal equation of state. We then reconstruct nonlinear black-brane geometries and the scalar potential using thermodynamics, ultraviolet asymptotics, Ward identities, and horizon regularity. Independent solutions of the bulk Einstein-scalar equations demonstrate that accurately reproducing thermodynamics with a trained PINN does not guarantee an accurate reconstruction of the scalar potential. High-precision knowledge of the high-temperature equation of state constrains nonlinear interactions in the bulk scalar potential. Fixing the cubic coupling to its exact PW value, motivated by this high-temperature extraction, reduces the maximum sampled error in the reconstructed scalar self-interactions by a factor of $\sim 15$ compared with constraining only the bulk scalar mass. Adding knowledge of the bulk viscosity of the gauge theory plasma further reduces this error by an additional factor of $\sim 13$, with independent forward solutions reproducing the bulk viscosity within $0.09\%$.
papers.summary: The paper applies physics‑informed neural networks to the bosonic sector of the Pilch–Warner N=2* holographic model, successfully reproducing the high‑temperature equation of state and reconstructing nonlinear black‑brane geometries and the scalar potential. By fixing the cubic coupling to its exact value and incorporating bulk viscosity data, the authors reduce errors in the scalar self‑interactions by more than an order of magnitude, demonstrating that accurate thermodynamics does not automatically guarantee a precise bulk reconstruction.

papers.title: Bondi Four-Momentum Balance in Quantum NSF Classical matching, DKL supermomentum, and quantum energy redistribution
papers.abstract: We derive Bondi four-momentum balance between past and future null infinity in the radiative phase space of the null-surface formulation (NSF). Weyl matching at spatial infinity, together with vanishing endpoint News, gives antipodal continuity of the Bondi mass aspect. Its translation projection is independent of the infrared shear term and transforms as a Lorentz four-vector. Bondi evolution relates the incoming and outgoing News fluxes to the timelike endpoint momenta; in the Dominguez--Kozameh--Ludvigsen radiative sector these momenta vanish and the fluxes are equal. On a common radiative Fock domain, unitary conjugation transports the flux observables. Adopting their classical balance as an additional quantum condition yields exclusive four-momentum conservation. We also calculate the outgoing energy expectation without imposing that condition. For an incoming energy eigenstate, the second-generator commutator vanishes diagonally, leaving a second-order coefficient determined by the cubic generator. Direct canonical contractions isolate the contribution connected to all four external legs. For the equal-energy center-of-mass preparation, axial rotational covariance forces the angularly integrated exchange coefficient to vanish under the finite helicity-projection prescription of Part~I. The connected energy defect therefore vanishes through second order. The full expectation (including spectators) and higher-order balance remain open.
papers.summary: The paper establishes a quantum version of the Bondi four‑momentum balance by matching radiative data at past and future null infinity within the null‑surface formulation, showing that the fluxes of incoming and outgoing News are equal under certain conditions and that the resulting four‑momentum is conserved in a unitary Fock domain. It further computes the expectation value of outgoing energy for an incoming eigenstate, demonstrating that the leading‑order energy defect vanishes and outlining a framework for higher‑order corrections.

papers.title: A critical coupling for the magnetic instability of holographic SU(2) plasmas
papers.abstract: We show that gravity can remove the linear magnetic instability of a holographic plasma with an $SU(2)$ global symmetry. In the probe limit, charged vector bosons become tachyonic in their lowest Landau level above a critical field and condense into a vortex lattice. In Einstein-$SU(2)$ Yang-Mills theory in AdS$_5$ we include the backreaction of the field exactly, expanding only in the condensate around the D'Hoker-Kraus magnetic brane. The critical field diverges as the coupling $\alpha = \kappa^2/\hat g^2$ approaches $\alpha_\star = 2/3$, above which the normal phase has no linear charged instability at any field or temperature: we show this at zero temperature and establish it numerically at finite temperature. At zero temperature the field cancels from the mass of the lowest Landau level in the brane's AdS$_3 \times \mathbb{R}^2$ throat, and the instability is a violation of the throat's Breitenlohner-Freedman bound. The onset temperature vanishes at $\alpha_\star$ with an essential singularity of Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless type. For two-derivative Einstein-Yang-Mills duals in $d = 4$, 5 and 6 dimensions the normal phase has a charged instability if and only if $C_J/C_T < 8/(d^2(d+1))$, one tenth in $d = 4$. Above $\alpha_L = 0.372$ the gravitational attraction between vortices makes the uniform lattice unstable and the transition first order, so $B_c$ is only a spinodal; whether a condensed phase survives above $\alpha_\star$ is left open.
papers.summary: The authors analyze the magnetic instability of a holographic SU(2) plasma in Einstein–Yang–Mills theory, showing that backreaction can eliminate the tachyonic Landau level and identifying a critical coupling α∗=2/3 beyond which the normal phase is stable at all fields and temperatures. They further map the onset temperature to a BKT‑type essential singularity and discuss the first‑order transition induced by vortex interactions above another threshold αL≈0.372.

papers.title: Charged Deformation of a Hairy Black Brane: Perturbative Solution and Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We study electrically charged black branes in four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with Maxwell coupling $Z(\phi)=e^{3\phi/\sqrt7}$, whose potential has an AdS$_4$ fixed point only in the infrared. For nonzero hair parameter $\alpha$ the scalar grows logarithmically at large radius and the geometry is not asymptotically AdS, so the holographic dictionary is a working assumption. With the scale-invariant multi-trace boundary condition of the neutral branes, giving conformal thermodynamics, we work to second order in the charge, obtaining the Maxwell field and susceptibility in closed form, plus the thermodynamics, condensate, incoherent conductivity and cumulant ratio $T^2\chi_4/\chi_2=6c(\alpha)<0$ for all $\alpha$ considered. Independent perturbative computations and first-law closed forms agree within $4\times10^{-6}$; nonlinear solutions reproduce second-order results to $1.2\times10^{-5}$ and $c$ to $6\times10^{-4}$. They are locally thermodynamically stable where constructed, and the pressure is analytic in $(\mu_Q/T)^2$ near zero density. No regular extremal horizon exists at finite scalar value, and $\rho/s<\sqrt{21}/(2\pi)$ exactly. The extremal limit is an AdS$_2\times\mathbb R^2$ throat where the scalar grows as $\ln\ln(1/u)$ in the AdS$_2$ radial coordinate $u$; the bound is saturated there, and extremal values are approached as powers of $1/\ln(\mu_Q/T)$. With a Dirichlet condition on the scalar source, the same solutions describe a non-conformal theory with scale $\Lambda$, whose charged branes exist only below $T_{\max}(\mu_Q)$, which falls from $0.194\Lambda$ at zero density to zero at $\mu_Q=0.506\Lambda$. This boundary is a diffusive instability where the charge susceptibility diverges at nonzero density, and the bulk viscosity violates Buchel's bound at all densities. Quasinormal modes with the normalizable large-radius condition reproduce its hydrodynamics.
papers.summary: This work constructs perturbative charged black brane solutions in a four‑dimensional Einstein‑Maxwell‑scalar theory with a non‑AdS asymptotic scalar profile, and derives their thermodynamics, transport coefficients, and extremal limits. The analysis reveals a universal bound on charge density, a non‑conformal phase transition, and a violation of the bulk‑viscosity bound, offering new insights into holographic models of non‑relativistic matter.

papers.title: Holographic theory of non-invertible gravitational anomalies
papers.abstract: We review a many-body formulation of gravitational anomalies as obstructions to realizing the complete low-energy data by a local {\it bosonic} lattice quantum system of the same dimension. In this formulation, an anomalous theory can be realized at the boundary of a gapped {\it bosonic} lattice bulk, whose topological order gives a one-to-one classification of the anomaly. An invertible bulk reproduces conventional anomaly inflow; a bulk with non-trivial topological excitations yields a non-invertible generalization. To describe the holographic theory of anomalies, we explain the distinction between uniquely defined topological order and many versions of topological quantum field theory and discuss the boundary-to-bulk map. As an application of the holographic theory of anomalies, we describe morphisms between local quantum theories (such as quantum field theories). These morphisms are built from a bulk domain wall and an invertible boundary junction, which give rise to a sandwich picture. Chiral boson/fermion theory, Laughlin edges, and boundaries of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ higher gauge theory with bosonic or fermionic point-like excitations illustrate the different kinds of information about non-invertible anomalies contained in transport coefficients, superselection sectors, and condensation data. In particular, a fermionic theory can be viewed as a theory with a particular non-invertible gravitational anomaly. Those examples also reveal that {\it symmetry $\sim$ gravitational anomaly $\sim$ topological order in one higher dimension}.
papers.summary: This paper develops a holographic framework for classifying gravitational anomalies via gapped bosonic lattice bulks, showing that non‑invertible anomalies correspond to bulks with nontrivial topological excitations. It applies this perspective to concrete models—chiral bosons, Laughlin edges, and $mathbb{Z}_2$ higher‑gauge boundaries—to illustrate how transport, superselection, and condensation data encode anomaly information.

papers.title: Rank polarization and dynamical autonomy in a projective rotor model
papers.abstract: We study how a higher-rank classical collective order parameter can select one dominant projective eigenline and, in a $p=2$ realization, support a dynamically autonomous low-energy director sector. In a fully connected projective-rotor model, the collective second moment is a positive semidefinite tensor $T$ of fixed trace. Conventional projective ordering drives its effective rank toward one, selecting a single dominant eigenline. Rank polarization alone, however, does not determine dynamical autonomy: extrinsic-curvature criteria depend on the chosen state-space metric, and the equilibrium tensor does not determine the transverse free-energy Hessian. A two-harmonic model makes this logical independence explicit by producing families with identical $T$ and $r_{\rm eff}$ but different transverse quadratic forms. We then construct rotationally invariant locking interactions that leave a prescribed ordered tensor exactly fixed while increasing every non-Goldstone restoring coefficient as $\Theta(\lambda)$ within a globally controlled stable regime. For a phenomenological inertial realization with a finite positive kinetic matrix, the lowest transverse normal-mode frequency grows as $\Theta(\lambda^{1/2})$; more generally, the low-frequency transverse susceptibility is suppressed as $O(\lambda^{-1})$, including in overdamped dynamics. The construction therefore proves that spectral selection and infrared transverse suppression are independent data. For $p>2$ the selected eigenline has a $(p-1)$-dimensional director manifold; the one-dimensional Goldstone sector used in the dynamical construction is specific to $p=2$. Promoting the selected internal eigenline to a physical clock requires additional soldering and integrability structure.
papers.summary: This paper investigates how a higher-rank classical order parameter in a fully connected projective rotor model can select a dominant eigenline and achieve dynamical autonomy in the low-energy director sector. It demonstrates that spectral selection and infrared transverse suppression are independent, using rotationally invariant locking interactions and a phenomenological inertial realization.

papers.title: Phase transitions and quasinormal modes of Euler-Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes
papers.authors: Yi-Qi Chen, De-Cheng Zou, Ming Zhang, Xufen Zhang, Bo Liu, Rui-Hong Yue
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study phase transitions and scalar quasinormal modes(QNMs) of magnetically charged Euler--Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes in the extended phase space. We classify the horizon structures for all three signs of the EH coupling and derive the extended first law when the pressure and coupling are varied. For negative coupling, the physical branch exhibits a Van der Waals-like small/large black-hole transition. Using the improved asymptotic iteration method, we find two separated QNM trajectories below the critical pressure, whereas they merge into one continuous curve at the critical point. The GHS limit and the positive couplings considered here do not produce a finite-radius critical point.
papers.summary: This paper investigates the thermodynamic phase structure and quasinormal mode spectra of magnetically charged Euler–Heisenberg–dilaton AdS black holes, finding a Van der Waals–like small/large black hole transition for negative coupling. Using the improved asymptotic iteration method, the authors map QNM trajectories that split below the critical pressure and merge at the critical point, while the GHS limit and positive couplings lack a finite‑radius critical point.

papers.title: Aspects of $\mathcal{N}=2$ SUSY gauge theories and applications to Quantum Field Theory and Gravity
papers.abstract: This thesis investigates the application of techniques developed in supersymmetric gauge theories to physical problems in Quantum Field Theory and Gravity, focusing on the Seiberg-Witten (SW) curve and its quantum version. After reviewing the essential concepts of Supersymmetry and the derivation of the SW curve, we explore its applications in both fields. In Quantum Field Theory, we investigate the emergence of Argyres-Douglas theories in the moduli space of supersymmetric models, focusing on extremal correlators. We analyze a conformal model to compute their instanton corrections, finding agreement with predictions from Effective Field Theory, and discuss the implications for analogous observables in Argyres-Douglas theories. In Gravity, we exploit the quantum SW curve and its relation to differential equations describing physical systems. We establish the linear stability of Topological Stars, arising in the fuzzball proposal, under massive charged scalar perturbations. We also investigate charge superradiance in configurations with a horizon and derive a novel hypergeometric representation of the confluent Heun function, relevant to gravitational-wave propagation in the Schwarzschild background. This result yields a new resummed expression for waveform tail contributions, in excellent agreement with numerical data. Finally, beyond the SW formalism, we develop a Machine Learning algorithm based on Hamiltonian Neural Networks to reproduce the geodesics of a neutral particle in a fuzzball geometry. For critical trajectories, our method outperforms standard numerical integrators in both efficiency and accuracy.
papers.summary: The thesis applies Seiberg-Witten techniques to study Argyres-Douglas theories and quantum corrections in supersymmetric gauge models, and extends the quantum SW curve to analyze stability of fuzzball geometries and gravitational-wave tails. It also introduces a Hamiltonian neural network to efficiently reproduce particle geodesics in a fuzzball background.

papers.title: New topological phase transitions in $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice models
papers.abstract: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/\alpha^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.
papers.summary: The paper studies a momentum‑space topological phase transition in a κ‑deformed φ^4 lattice model, showing that the double‑well structure leads to degenerate high‑energy momentum states and a transition governed by a 1/α^4 power law. Numerical and singularity‑theory analyses confirm the result and predict a nonzero fraction of particles in degenerate states even in the commutative limit, offering a testable signature of noncommutative spacetime.

papers.title: Higher Dressing and Shift-Invariance in 4D Topological BF Theory
papers.abstract: A characteristic feature of topological field theories is the absence of local propagating degrees of freedom. In four-dimensional BF theory with cosmological term, we make this feature manifest by exactly reducing the finite non-Abelian shift symmetry. We do so by identifying a higher dressing field, a 1-form compensating the shift, allowing to build from first principles the composite shift-invariant field $\boldsymbol{B}=B-\lambda^{-1}F$. In terms of this dressed field, the dynamics becomes algebraic and sets $\boldsymbol{B}=0$, directly exposing the absence of local propagating degrees of freedom. This provides the first explicit instance of the higher-form Dressing Field Method.
papers.summary: The authors introduce a higher-form dressing field in 4D BF theory with a cosmological term, allowing them to construct a composite shift-invariant field that renders the dynamics algebraic and forces it to vanish, thereby making the absence of local degrees of freedom explicit. This work provides the first explicit application of the higher-form Dressing Field Method, offering a new perspective on shift symmetries in topological field theories.

papers.title: Area metric gravity \`a la Plebanski: connection, curvature and dynamics
papers.abstract: Area metrics arise as effective description at intermediate scales in a number of approaches to quantum gravity, including string theory, holography and loop quantum gravity. Recently, it has been shown that area metric actions can be derived from the modified Plebanski framework on the linearized level. Surprisingly these actions avoid extra poles in the propagator for the effective length dynamics, and hence constitute interesting deformations of linearized Einstein gravity. To be able to study whether this property persist for the full theory, we construct here non-linear area metric dynamics from modified Plebanski actions. We provide the geometric tools for area metrics that do not rely on perturbation theory and allow a systematic construction and study of general non-linear area metric actions: an algorithm that extracts a length metric from an area metric and a connection on two-forms that is uniquely determined by the area metric, together with its curvature and curvature invariants. We derive area metric actions from modified Plebanski actions in first and second order versions. We also find that area metric actions can be reformulated as Poincare gauge theories. We determine the effective length metric action, which on a flat background describes a graviton and a massive spin-two field with parity-violating couplings set by the Barbero--Immirzi parameter. Additionally we discuss cosmological backgrounds and the role of the matter coupling, which together open the way to cosmological applications.
papers.summary: The authors construct non‑linear area metric dynamics from modified Plebanski actions, providing a systematic geometric framework that yields effective length metric actions describing a graviton and a massive spin‑two field with parity‑violating couplings. These results open a path toward cosmological applications and suggest new deformations of Einstein gravity that avoid extra propagator poles.

papers.title: From Lyapunov Growth to Weak Quantum Chaos
papers.abstract: Local out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) measure the growth of initially small commutators. For bounded local operators, this growth ends when the local commutator becomes of order one, but in an extended system the region over which it is large can continue to expand. We study this spatial proliferation using three related observables: the local squared commutator $C_r(t)$, its spatial sum $\bar C(t) = \sum_r C_r(t)$, and the symmetrically regularised connected dOTOC $D(t)$ of two extensive observables. We show that Lieb--Robinson locality gives $\bar C(t) \lesssim t^d$. We then prove that, in a Gibbs state with uniform exponential clustering, the full dOTOC obeys the same bound, $D(t) \lesssim t^d$, improving our earlier suboptimal $t^{3d}$ bound. We illustrate these results in two quantum many-body systems: a Brownian coupled-cluster model and a finite-temperature SYK chain. In both cases, an exact disorder symmetry relates $D(t)$ to $\bar C(t)$ and allows us to follow the same extensive observable from the pre-scrambling Lyapunov regime into the post-scrambling growth associated with an expanding saturated region. This late-time power-law growth is the concrete realisation of the weak quantum chaos introduced in our earlier work.
papers.summary: This work extends the study of out-of-time-order correlators by proving that the spatially summed squared commutator and the connected dOTOC grow at most polynomially in time, with a bound set by Lieb–Robinson locality. The authors illustrate the result in a Brownian coupled‑cluster model and a finite‑temperature SYK chain, showing how the extensive observable evolves from Lyapunov growth to a late‑time power‑law regime characteristic of weak quantum chaos.

papers.title: Microscopic entropy of regular BTZ black holes in 3d Lovelock gravity at all orders
papers.abstract: We give a microscopic derivation of the semi-classical entropy of the black holes of 3d Lovelock gravity with an infinite tower of regularized Lovelock corrections, which include the regular BTZ black holes found recently. Working in the mini-superspace formalism, we show that the reduced action and its boundary term can be obtained in closed form at all orders in terms of the generating function of the couplings. Assuming the ground state is described by the soliton obtained from the static black hole by a double Wick rotation, we compute the soliton mass and reproduce the semi-classical entropy from the Cardy formula without central charges for arbitrary couplings. We then extend the mini-superspace to stationary configurations, compute the mass and the angular momentum of the rotating black holes obtained by a boost, and verify the Cardy formula in the presence of rotation.
papers.summary: The authors derive the entropy of regular BTZ black holes in 3d Lovelock gravity with an infinite series of corrections using a mini‑superspace approach, reproducing the Cardy formula without central charges. They extend the analysis to rotating solutions, computing mass and angular momentum via a boost and confirming the Cardy relation in the rotating case.

papers.title: Random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries
papers.abstract: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). In contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). We discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone BPS states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. Finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.
papers.summary: This work investigates how momentum fractionation in smooth 3‑charge superstrata influences chaotic dynamics of null geodesics and waves, finding that fractionated backgrounds exhibit strong, Berry‑random‑wave‑like chaos while single‑mode geometries remain closer to integrable behavior. The authors suggest that the reduced chaos in monotone BPS states may reflect a deeper distinction between generic and special microstates, and argue that their probes remain informative even as the geometries approach the black‑hole limit.

papers.title: Symmetric Dual Breather Modes as a Dynamic Origin of Tiny Particle Masses
papers.abstract: Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) is conventionally understood through static vacuum selection in low-energy approximations. However, the nonperturbative dynamical pathways connecting symmetric configurations to asymmetric states remain an open question. In this paper, we propose an operator-theoretic framework that characterizes $Z_{2}$ symmetry breaking in scalar field theory through spectral branching. Specifically, we identify an effective invariant manifold of the nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation termed the "symmetric dual breather mode," whose phase-space geometry is traced using a $t$-dependent finite-dimensional representation. Our analysis demonstrates that static SSB represents merely a small-amplitude limit ($A \ll \phi_{v1}$). As the amplitude increases into the heteroclinic regime ($A > \phi_{v1}$), the field dynamically overflows the central barrier, yielding a vanishing time-averaged order parameter ($\langle \phi \rangle = 0$) and driving a geometric curvature cancellation ($\langle V''(\phi) \rangle_{t} \to 0$). Governed by a universal scaling function $\mathfrak{F}(y)$, the logarithmic period divergence near the heteroclinic boundary naturally generates sub-eV effective mass scales without fine-tuning bare parameters. Furthermore, this dynamic barrier overflow naturally favors Majorana-like self-conjugate states over Dirac-type states. Additionally, nonlinear phase interference along the heteroclinic channel induces asymmetric phase-space contraction, decoupling the right-handed mode and dynamically giving rise to the left-handed Weyl equation. These results bridge nonperturbative wave dynamics, topological mass suppression, chiral selection, and the dynamic origin of active neutrino masses.
papers.summary: This work proposes an operator-theoretic framework for dynamical spontaneous symmetry breaking in scalar field theory, identifying a symmetric dual breather mode that drives the field over the potential barrier and generates sub-eV mass scales via a universal scaling function. The analysis further suggests that this dynamic barrier overflow naturally selects Majorana-like self-conjugate states and produces chiral asymmetry, offering a nonperturbative route to active neutrino masses.

papers.title: Relativistic Covariance from Hamiltonian Hydrodynamics in the Chiral Limit
papers.abstract: We derive the covariant equations of nondissipative chiral hydrodynamics from their equal-time Hamiltonian formulation and identify the Lie--Poisson structure implicit in the chiral brackets. This structure combines fluid motion with local chiral transformations. For a parity-invariant Hamiltonian quadratic in chiral charge densities and pion gradients, without external backgrounds, we derive and solve the constraints imposed by Lorentz boosts. Their coupled nonlinear sector is equivalent to the linear boost transformation laws of a symmetric tensor, which determine the velocity dependence from rest-frame data. For finite, positive rest-frame coefficients, finite ordinary-fluid energy density and thermodynamic derivatives, and a momentum--velocity relation that can be solved in either direction, the chiral Hamiltonian coefficients remain finite at every fluid speed below light speed if and only if the rest-frame pion propagation speed does not exceed the speed of light. This formulation makes symmetry constraints explicit and provides a starting point for future thermodynamically consistent dissipative extensions.
papers.summary: The paper derives covariant, nondissipative chiral hydrodynamic equations from an equal‑time Hamiltonian framework, revealing a Lie–Poisson structure that intertwines fluid motion with local chiral transformations. It shows that Lorentz‑boost constraints enforce that the pion propagation speed remains subluminal, ensuring finite Hamiltonian coefficients for all fluid velocities below light speed.

papers.title: Retarded Green Function For Bopp--Podolsky Electrodynamics in Four-Dimensional De Sitter Spacetime
papers.abstract: We study classical Bopp--Podolsky (BP) electrodynamics on four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime, focusing on its transverse retarded Green function and gauge-invariant electromagnetic response. Because de Sitter spacetime is maximally symmetric, its vector Green functions admit a covariant expansion in a finite basis of invariant bitensors, with scalar coefficients depending only on the invariant separation. For conserved sources, the fourth-order field operator factorizes into Maxwell and massive-vector operators, yielding the BP retarded kernel as the difference of their transverse Green functions. Using the invariant bitensor decomposition, we reduce the propagator equations to a hypergeometric master equation and determine the distributional structure of its solution. The common leading short-distance singularity of the Maxwell and massive-vector sectors cancels, leaving a logarithmic master singularity and a softened vector-potential wavefront. After one curl, the gauge-invariant field-strength kernel contains a null-cone delta distribution and a regular timelike tail. The smooth Maxwell master tail is annihilated by the curl, so the interior electromagnetic tail is generated entirely by the massive sector. We also derive an exact horizon-regular static potential, demonstrate the cancellation of the Coulomb divergence, recover the flat-space BP potential, and formulate the generalized Gauss law. On global de Sitter spacetime, the compactness of the spatial sections requires the total charge to vanish; we implement this constraint using an antipodal charge configuration with smooth factorized initial data. The analysis is classical and does not assume a quantum Lee--Wick contour or a preferred de Sitter vacuum.
papers.summary: The paper derives the transverse retarded Green function for Bopp–Podolsky electrodynamics on four‑dimensional de Sitter space, showing that the fourth‑order field operator factorizes into Maxwell and massive‑vector parts and that their leading singularities cancel, leaving a softened vector‑potential wavefront and a logarithmic master singularity. It further constructs an exact horizon‑regular static potential, demonstrates Coulomb divergence cancellation, and imposes a vanishing total charge on global de Sitter via an antipodal charge configuration.

papers.title: A first order nonabelian antisymmetric tensor model with hidden higher symmetry
papers.abstract: We present a nonabelian complex self-dual antisymmetric tensor model, with gauged internal symmetry, comprising a complex multiplet of massless self-dual antisymmetric tensor fields and its conjugate (interacting with massless Yang-Mills gauge fields). We build the model at the classical level, via a first order formulation, assigning local fields to a component expansion over the Dirac algebra and a basis of internal matrices, with Lorentz and gauge invariance ensured by tracing, and applying an appropriate bilinear form. The full expansion requires auxiliary place-holder fields, which are not potentials, but become curvatures (field strengths) after elimination via their algebraic equations of motion. The component expansion over the Dirac algebra is closed under multiplication by additional internal matrices, which are not gauge group generators, but mix internal components, and link auxiliary curvatures with potentials. The model is shown to be invariant under such transformations, and thus possesses a type of hidden internal symmetry. We analyze the specific case of gauge group $SU(2)\! \times \! U(1)$, and as higher symmetry candidates, we consider both the Lie group $SU(3)$ and the Lie superalgebra $SU(2/1)$ (with the additional matrices acting via Lie brackets, or graded Lie brackets, respectively).
papers.summary: This paper constructs a first‑order formulation of a non‑abelian complex self‑dual antisymmetric tensor field coupled to Yang‑Mills gauge fields, using a Dirac‑algebra component expansion and auxiliary curvatures that are eliminated algebraically. The authors uncover a hidden internal symmetry generated by additional matrices that mix the tensor multiplet components, and explore extensions to SU(3) and the superalgebra SU(2/1) as higher‑symmetry candidates.

papers.title: Regular-Zero Drinfeld-Sokolov Charges in Doubled Four-Dimensional Chern-Simons Theory
papers.authors: Wentao Zeng, Yifan He, Xian Wu
papers.abstract: We study classical local conserved charges obtained after finite-defect reduction of doubled four-dimensional Chern--Simons theory. At a finite simple zero, the inhomogeneous derivative term in the affine gauge transformation induced by the twist function vanishes, so the residue evaluations of the two Gaudin currents transform by the ordinary adjoint action. For each simple ideal, we use the Evans-compatible invariant tensors of the principal Drinfeld--Sokolov hierarchy as external algebraic input, construct local circle integrals, and treat the same-zero, distinct-zero, and mixed sectors separately, proving pairwise Poisson commutativity. Under the explicit assumptions of Stedman's simple-pole/simple-zero boundary Hamiltonian, the periodic trivial-monodromy sector, and boundary weights independent of phase-space variables, the reduced Hamiltonian decomposes term by term into finite-pole, infinity, finite-zero, and residual first-class-constraint contributions, which yields conservation of the constructed charges. We distinguish the finite-defect reduced space, the extended space carrying the residual constraint, and the physical quotient. The result is a conditional existence statement for a classical local Abelian Poisson subalgebra; we make no claim of functional independence, maximality, or Liouville completeness. Extensions to higher-order zeros and nontrivial monodromy sectors are outside the scope of this work.
papers.summary: This paper constructs classical local conserved charges in a finite-defect reduction of doubled four-dimensional Chern–Simons theory, using Drinfeld–Sokolov hierarchies and Gaudin currents to prove Poisson commutativity of the resulting charges. The analysis is limited to simple zeros and trivial monodromy, leaving extensions to higher-order zeros and nontrivial sectors for future work.

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Nonspherical Bounces with a Single Negative Mode
papers.authors: Guangshang Chen, Jianpeng Dai, Yang Xiao
papers.abstract: False vacuum decay is conventionally described by a spherically symmetric bounce with a single negative fluctuation mode. This raises a fundamental question: can the single negative mode requirement itself enforce spherical symmetry, independently of action minimization? For a single real scalar field with a smooth potential in flat spacetime, we rigorously prove that every localized nonspherical saddle with zero initial velocity has at least three negative modes. Additional reflection symmetries further tighten these bounds, as illustrated in a sextic scalar model. Our findings exclude nonspherical bounce candidates with a single negative mode, providing a complementary spectral foundation for the spherical bounce description of false vacuum decay.
papers.summary: The paper proves that any nonspherical bounce solution with zero initial velocity in a single real scalar field theory must have at least three negative fluctuation modes, thereby ruling out nonspherical bounces with a single negative mode. This result supports the conventional spherical bounce picture of false vacuum decay by providing a spectral constraint independent of action minimization.

papers.title: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
papers.abstract: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.
papers.summary: This paper reviews Volovich's 1987 work on p‑adic string theory and the subsequent development of Feynman rules for the p‑adic string and its associated non‑local field theory, highlighting their applications in various physical contexts. The authors also share recollections of visits to Moscow in the late 1980s and early 1990s, providing historical context for the field.

papers.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
papers.authors: A. Ramesh Chandra, Aaghaz Mahajan, Ainesh Sanyal, Mianqi Wang, Shubhadeep Chakraborty, Sudip Chakraborty, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Rama Govindarajan, Akshit Goyal, Jonathan J. Heckman, Yasir Iqbal, Divya Jaganathan, Saumav Kapoor, Andreas Karch, Pushkar Khandare, Sandeep Krishna, Anupam Kundu, Alok Laddha, Tongyan Lin, Swarnendu Maity, Nilmani Mathur, Shani Nadir Meynet, Alessandro Mininno, Abhijeet Mishra, Vidur Niranjan, Abhishodh Prakash, Pratik Rath, Durbar Roy, Debargha Sarkar, Srikanth Sastry, Gary Shiu, Aninda Sinha, Thomas Van Riet, Praneeth Netrapalli, Suvrat Raju
papers.abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a benchmark of 50 theoretical physics problems and evaluates state‑of‑the‑art AI agents on them, achieving 98 % accuracy with modest cost. It highlights the agents’ strong memorization of physics literature and discusses why such performance has not yet led to breakthrough discoveries.

papers.title: Out-of-time-order hydrodynamics and scrambling
papers.authors: Marta Bucca, Akash Jain, M\'ark Mezei, Alexey Milekhin
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamics as an effective field theory (EFT) has been immensely successful for predicting the behaviour of time-ordered correlation functions in the long-time, large-distance regime. In this paper, we analyse the predictions of hydrodynamics for scrambling as probed by out-of-time order correlators (OTOCs). To do so, we consider an all-derivative order generalisation of the Schwinger-Keldysh EFT of hydrodynamics extended to a four-fold time contour required to capture OTOCs. A crucial ingredient of the construction is a local SL(2,R) symmetry, which has previously been suggested as a mechanism for scrambling. We also derive this exact EFT from the microscopic formulation of the maximally chaotic low-temperature limit of the SYK lattice, thereby determining all transport coefficients for this model. As a novel application, we compute the OTOC of energy currents, find that its exponential growth saturates the chaos bound, and match it to expectations based on a shockwave (or scramblon) effective description. Our work shows that the universality of hydrodynamics degrees of freedom extends beyond traditional time-ordered correlators to more complex observables such as OTOCs.
papers.summary: This paper extends the Schwinger‑Keldysh effective field theory of hydrodynamics to a four‑fold contour to compute out‑of‑time‑order correlators, revealing that the energy‑current OTOC grows exponentially and saturates the chaos bound. By matching the EFT to the low‑temperature SYK lattice, the authors determine all transport coefficients and confirm that the shockwave (scramblon) picture reproduces the same scrambling dynamics.

papers.title: Metric and dilaton information from high-overtone quasinormal modes of analytic Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black holes
papers.authors: Yu Shi, Chikun Ding, Yuebing Zhou, Changqing Liu, Weike Deng, Sheng Long
papers.abstract: Black-hole interiors are hidden from exterior observers, yet their geometry can enter the high-overtone spectrum of linear perturbations. We study how this spectrum encodes metric and supporting-matter information in analytic Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes. Coupling a neutral spectator to the dilaton at fixed UV dimension provides a matter-sensitive channel alongside the momentum response. For real-endpoint spacelike connections, the momentum response and mass-label dependence separate the metric exponents from the signed dilaton slope. Near the causal threshold, a complex endpoint controls the spectral family: the mass profiles approach a common value, producing a shared fractional correction, while regular propagation retains label dependence. This mechanism is present at criticality without an inner horizon and continues locally into timelike interiors. Exterior numerical spectra support the reconstruction and the leading complex-endpoint responses. Local scaling and probe coupling set the candidate responses, while wave connection determines their imprint on the exterior spectrum.
papers.summary: This work investigates how the high-overtone quasinormal mode spectrum of analytic Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton black holes encodes interior metric and dilaton information. By coupling a neutral spectator to the dilaton and analyzing momentum response and mass-label dependence, the authors demonstrate a reconstruction scheme that can be tested against exterior numerical spectra.

papers.title: Modular Flow and Holographic Timelike Entanglement Entropy in AdS and Flat Holography
papers.authors: Mehdi Hakami Shalamzari, Zahra Paygozar, Mahdi Kord Zangeneh
papers.abstract: Timelike entanglement entropy provides a useful probe of holographic theoris, yet an explicit bulk realization of the modular flow underlying its timelike extremal curve construction has so far been lacking. We construct modular flows associated with spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ and extend this framework to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$. Beginning with the boundary symmetry generators, we explicitly derive the boundary modular flows and extend them into the bulk, providing a systematic procedure that relates bulk modular flows to the extremal curves and holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy.   For spacelike intervals, the resulting bulk modular flows determine the extremal curves, whose integrated line elements reproduce the standard holographic entanglement entropy. We then generalize this approach to timelike intervals, explicitly constructing the modular flows whose fixed points reproduce the extremal spacelike and timelike curves which gives the holographic timelike entanglement entropy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first explicit construction of the modular flow associated with a timelike extremal curve for a timelike interval.   The same procedure is then carried over to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$, which give rise to the holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. Finally, we show that the flat space results obtained in this work can be recovered from their AdS$_3$ counterparts in the flat space limit.
papers.summary: This paper constructs explicit bulk modular flows for both spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ and extends the construction to flat$_3$/CCFT$_2$, showing how the flows generate the corresponding extremal curves that compute holographic entanglement entropy, including the novel timelike case. The authors also demonstrate that the flat-space results arise as a flat-space limit of the AdS$_3$ results, providing a unified framework for timelike entanglement in holography.

papers.title: On the analytic continuation and asymptotic behaviour of the two-point function in massless $\phi^4$-theory in Euclidean de Sitter space
papers.abstract: For the two-point function of the massless, minimally-coupled, real scalar field in Euclidean de Sitter space with $\lambda\phi^4$-interaction, we compute the leading-logarithmic terms in the invariant distance of the two-point function to $O(\lambda^2)$, which counts as the fifth subleading order (N$^5$LO) in the $\sqrt{\lambda}$-expansion. We show that the analytic continuation to Lorentzian signature coincides with the expansion of the analogous quantity computed in the stochastic formalism. We determine the large-order behaviour of the stochastic series expansion and prove its Borel summability, which suggests that the Euclidean theory can be used to extract the late-time behaviour of massless correlation functions in Lorentzian de Sitter space.
papers.summary: This work computes the leading-logarithmic corrections to the two-point function of a massless scalar with quartic self-interaction in Euclidean de Sitter space up to order λ^2, showing that its analytic continuation matches the stochastic approach. The authors also analyze the large-order behavior of the stochastic series, proving Borel summability and suggesting that Euclidean results can inform late-time Lorentzian correlators.

papers.title: New analytic Janus and $S^4$ solutions for $\mathcal{N}=2^*$
papers.abstract: We construct a three-parameter family of regular analytic supergravity solutions which are dual to (a) the $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ gauge theory on the four-sphere, and (b) $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$-invariant Janus interfaces in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM with or without the $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ mass turned on. To this end we employ a five-dimensional supergravity model coupled to six scalars which arises as a certain consistent truncation of type IIB supergravity on $S^5$. The curved domain wall solutions feature a hidden integral of motion which allows for their analytic treatment. We relate the three parameters of the solution to field theory sources and vevs and show how regularity of the solutions restricts their range. We briefly discuss the holographic evaluation of the one-point function of the field theory Lagrangian for our family of Janus solutions.
papers.summary: The authors construct a three‑parameter family of regular analytic five‑dimensional supergravity solutions that are holographically dual to (mathcal{N}=2^*) gauge theory on (S^4) and to (mathrm{U}(1)^2)-invariant Janus interfaces in (mathcal{N}=4) SYM, using a consistent truncation of type IIB on (S^5). They exploit a hidden integral of motion to solve the curved domain‑wall equations, relate the parameters to field‑theory sources and vevs, and discuss the holographic one‑point function of the Lagrangian.

papers.title: Holographic Pseudo Entropy from the Rindler Method in AdS and Flat Space
papers.authors: Mehdi Hakami Shalamzari, Zahra Paygozar, Mahdi Kord Zangeneh
papers.abstract: Via the Rindler method, we study holographic timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) for a general timelike interval in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ and flat$_3$/CCFT$_2$. The TEE is the pseudo entropy of a timelike interval. In the bulk, the imaginary part of the TEE comes from a timelike geodesic, but in the Rindler picture this geodesic has not been identified. After a Rindler transformation to a rotating BTZ black hole, the two spacelike extremal curves lie on the inner and outer horizons, and exchanging $l_u\leftrightarrow \ell l_\phi$ takes one to the other. We find the geometric meaning of the timelike extremal curve: a geodesic stretched between the two horizons. Its length, $i\pi\ell$, is independent of the interval, and it alone produces the imaginary part $i\pi c/6$. We follow the same procedure in flat space holography, where the spacelike curve sits on the cosmological horizon and the timelike curve lies between the cosmological horizon and timelike infinity. Evaluating the holographic TEE for a timelike interval in CCFT$_2$ on the plane, we find that, in contrast with the cylinder, the real and imaginary parts are equal.
papers.summary: The paper extends the Rindler method to compute holographic timelike entanglement entropy (pseudo entropy) for general timelike intervals in AdS3/CFT2 and flat3/CCFT2, revealing that the imaginary part originates from a geodesic stretched between inner and outer horizons. It also shows that in flat space the real and imaginary parts of the TEE are equal on the plane, offering new geometric insights into timelike extremal curves.

papers.title: Love at First Loop: Quantum Deformability of Near-Extremal Black Holes
papers.authors: Pablo A. Cano, Marina David, Roberto Emparan, Stefano Trezzi
papers.abstract: The static Love numbers of black holes vanish in classical, four-dimensional, asymptotically flat General Relativity. We study how this changes for the response of near-extremal Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes to a minimally coupled massless scalar, at energies where the Schwarzian mode of the near-horizon throat fluctuates strongly. The black hole then responds as a quantum system with a spectrum of states. Its static response is a polarizability, given by virtual transitions between them. For $\ell=0$ the static Love number vanishes, by the shift symmetry of the scalar, but for multipoles $\ell\geq1$ the static Love numbers are nonzero: the finite rotational energy of the spin-$\ell$ intermediate states spoils the cancellation responsible for the classical result. Since the throat no longer has a classical geometry from which to read off a tidal response, we define it through the retarded Green's function, and compute its full frequency dependence at leading order in $r_+\omega$. Its conservative part requires renormalization: the near-horizon theory fixes the coefficient of its logarithm, and with it a dependence on the energy that no local term can remove, while its finite local terms are matching data of the four-dimensional theory. The dissipative part is finite and scheme independent. For $\ell\geq1$, it vanishes at low frequencies when the energy is below the rotational gap, while at the gap threshold it becomes non-analytic in frequency and produces a late-time $t^{-3/2}$ tail.
papers.summary: The paper shows that near‑extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes acquire nonzero static Love numbers for multipoles ℓ≥1 due to quantum fluctuations of the near‑horizon Schwarzian mode, turning the black hole into a quantum system with a discrete spectrum of spin‑ℓ excitations. By computing the retarded Green’s function at leading order in r+ω, the authors extract both conservative and dissipative tidal responses, revealing a universal t^(−3/2) late‑time tail at the rotational gap.

papers.title: Gauge-Invariant Brout--Englert--Higgs Mechanism without Spontaneous Breaking of Local Gauge Symmetry: A Quantum-Reference-Frame Formulation
papers.abstract: The Brout--Englert--Higgs (BEH) mechanism can be formulated in gauge-invariant relational terms without assigning physical spontaneous breaking to a local gauge redundancy. We treat the gauge orientation of the Higgs field as dynamical internal reference data and describe the gauge connection relative to this Higgs frame. On a regular patch where the frame exists, the Higgs kinetic term induces a positive-semidefinite mass-squared quadratic form on the gauge-orbit directions and reproduces the standard tree-level vector masses. A complete Higgs frame yields a gauge-invariant relational connection, whereas a partial frame is defined only up to a stabilizer group $H$ and produces Higgs stiffness only along the coset directions $G/H$. In quantum field theory the normalized frame and relational connection are nonpolynomial composite variables; physical masses are therefore characterized through suitably renormalized gauge-invariant composite correlators, or through fully dressed operators in residual-charged sectors. Applying this construction to the electroweak theory, we show that the Higgs frame relationalizes the $SU(2)_L$ redundancy while leaving a residual electromagnetic $U(1)_{\rm em}$ Gauss law: $W^\pm$ and charged fermionic modes require electromagnetic dressing, whereas neutral channels admit local gauge-invariant interpolators. This formulation connects Higgs dressings, FMS composites, and internal quantum-reference-frame language while keeping local mass generation distinct from global symmetry realization and topological obstructions.
papers.summary: This paper reformulates the Brout–Englert–Higgs mechanism in a gauge‑invariant, relational framework by treating the Higgs field’s orientation as a dynamical reference frame, yielding gauge‑invariant composite operators that encode the usual vector boson masses. It shows how this construction applies to the electroweak sector, leaving a residual U(1)_em Gauss law and clarifying the role of dressing for charged versus neutral modes.

papers.title: Yang-Baxter deformed sigma models on $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$
papers.authors: Danila Alexandrov, Alexey Bychkov, Ivan Kalinichenko, Alexey Litvinov
papers.abstract: We study Yang--Baxter deformations of two-dimensional sigma models on compact symmetric spaces $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$, with particular emphasis on their ultraviolet behavior. We claim that the ultraviolet fixed point is described by the $\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb C)/\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb R)$ non-compact WZW model together with $N-1$ compact free bosons. We determine the leading correction to this fixed point and identify it with the perturbation generated by the corresponding screening currents. We also extend our construction to the broader class of symmetric spaces of maximal rank.
papers.summary: The authors analyze Yang–Baxter deformations of sigma models on the symmetric space SU(N)/SO(N) and show that the UV fixed point is a non‑compact SO(N,ℂ)/SO(N,ℝ) WZW model plus N−1 free bosons. They compute the leading irrelevant operator as a screening‑current perturbation and generalize the construction to all maximal‑rank symmetric spaces.

papers.title: Type I-II/II-I vortices from dimension-six self-interaction
papers.authors: A. Alonso-Izquierdo, A. Gonz\'{a}lez-Parra, K. Slawinska, A. Wereszczynski, T. Winyard
papers.abstract: We show that adding a dimension-six self-interaction to the Abelian-Higgs or Ginzburg Landau model results in a remarkable and rich structure of multi-vortex solutions. Besides the standard type I (attractive) and type II (repulsive) regimes, separated by the Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfeld limit (BPS), we identify two new possibilities: type I-II vortices, which attract at short distances and repel at long distances; and type II-I vortices, with the opposite behaviour. Specifically, within the type II-I regime, multi-vortex solutions form chunks of the Abrikosov lattice or clusters. Conversely, in the I-II regime, axially symmetric multi-vortices are stable; nevertheless, depending on the model parameters and topological charge (winding number), they can be either the ground state or not.
papers.summary: The paper studies how a dimension‑six self‑interaction in the Abelian‑Higgs model produces new vortex regimes beyond the standard type I/II, including type I‑II and II‑I behaviours. It shows that multi‑vortex configurations can form lattice‑like clusters or stable axially symmetric states depending on parameters and winding number.

papers.title: Evading the Swampland de Sitter Obstruction via Thermodynamic Duality-Induced Horizon Corrections in Unimodular Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the early-universe cosmological implications of Unimodular Gravity coupled to Power-Law Nonlinear Electrodynamics in the presence of quantum-corrected horizon thermodynamics derived from the principle of thermodynamic duality. By incorporating both logarithmic and inverse-area corrections to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, we derive modified Friedmann equations exhibiting novel $H^4$ and $H^6$ terms that represent genuine quantum gravity effects. We demonstrate that these higher-order corrections become dynamically significant in the high-energy regime of cosmic inflation, naturally modifying the slow-roll dynamics without requiring a fundamental inflaton potential. A comprehensive phase-space analysis reveals that the quantum corrections drive early-time de Sitter-like attractors, providing a robust mechanism for sustained inflationary expansion. Confronting the model with the Swampland program, we show that the correction factor $\mathcal{F}(H)$ modifies the effective slow-roll parameters, enabling the model to satisfy the Swampland de Sitter and Distance conjectures during the inflationary epoch. We calculate the inflationary observables, including the spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, and demonstrate that the model's predictions are in excellent agreement with the Planck 2018 observational constraints. Our results suggest that thermodynamic duality-induced horizon corrections offer a viable and testable pathway for realizing successful inflation within a well-motivated quantum-gravitational framework.
papers.summary: The paper studies unimodular gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics with quantum‑corrected horizon thermodynamics, deriving modified Friedmann equations that include H^4 and H^6 terms. These corrections drive a de Sitter‑like inflationary attractor and allow the model to satisfy Swampland constraints while matching Planck 2018 data.

papers.title: Resonant JPZ algebras and 3D Chern--Simons gravity
papers.authors: Remigiusz Durka, Nelson Merino, D. M. Pe\~nafiel
papers.abstract: In this work we construct three-dimensional Chern--Simons gravity theories for the six resonant $JPZ$ algebras generated by the Lorentz generators $J_a$, translations $P_a$, and an additional Lorentz-like generator $Z_a$. The resonance condition together with the Jacobi identities leaves precisely six configurations arising from the semigroup expansions. Our main result is that three of them, $B_4$, $\widetilde C_4$, and $C_4$, are isomorphic to $iso(2,1)\oplus so(2,1)$, although they yield different gravitational realizations when we keep the original $JPZ$ field identification fixed. For each case $JPZ$, we determine the invariant tensors, gauge curvatures, Chern--Simons action, field equations, and the corresponding maximal-rank coupling sectors. The field equations can be written in the compact form $\Omega_\sigma\mathbf F=0$, which makes explicit how the additional field $h^a$ contributes to the curvature, torsion, and the remaining gauge-curvature components. We use the direct-sum isomorphisms to classify the local metric sectors and to relate them to known global and asymptotic solutions, while keeping the gravitational interpretation tied to the original $(\omega,e,h)$ fields.
papers.summary: This paper constructs three-dimensional Chern–Simons gravity theories based on six resonant JPZ algebras, identifying three that are isomorphic to iso(2,1)⊕so(2,1) and deriving their invariant tensors, gauge curvatures, and CS actions. The authors analyze the resulting field equations, maximal-rank coupling sectors, and local metric structures, linking them to known global and asymptotic solutions within the (ω,e,h) field framework.

papers.title: Beyond the circle: current algebras, geometry and higher gauge structures
papers.authors: R. Campoamor-Stursberg, A. Marrani, M. Rausch de Traubenberg
papers.abstract: Replacing the circle by a manifold leads to current Lie algebras and their central and derivation extensions. We separate the coefficient algebra, harmonic analysis and geometric data. Differentials modulo exact forms describe central extensions; divergence-free vector fields give explicit cocycles, whose compatible derivations satisfy a stabilizer equation. Compact examples include the three-sphere and its current--Virasoro extension. We also explain the analytic qualifications for SL(2,R) and its symmetric space and the role of transported multiplication in soft geometries. The recent harmonic constructions of Campoamor-Stursberg, Marrani and Rausch de Traubenberg are compared with the cohomological work of Coquereaux, Frappat, Ragoucy and Sorba and Castellani's loop geometry and infinite-dimensional free differential algebras. A coefficient-algebra construction connects currents to higher brackets and clarifies the additional requirements of a dynamical theory. For Lie algebras of order F, central extensions obey coupled binary and symmetric F-ary conditions, with explicit examples and obstructions.
papers.summary: This work generalizes current algebras from the circle to arbitrary manifolds, constructing central and derivation extensions that include a current–Virasoro algebra on S^3. It further develops higher gauge structures and higher-arity Lie algebras, offering new tools for studying symmetry algebras in higher-dimensional CFTs.

papers.title: Construction and geometric properties of the fuzzy $CP^3$ onion
papers.abstract: We consider the matrix model of a seven-dimensional quantum space built from concentric fuzzy $CP^3$'s of increasing matrix size, and show that its continuum limit is the metric cone $C(CP^3)$ over $CP^3$, not flat $R^7$. Every ingredient is fixed before any comparison, so this geometry is a prediction rather than an input. The two geometries agree in the $s$ wave ($p=0$) but separate in the higher angular sectors (harmonics on $CP^3$ of degree $p\geq1$): in each sector tested, the spectrum of the free Laplacian converges at second order to that of the cone, and at 20480 layers the cone is matched to $1\times10^{-9}$ for $p\leq8$, whereas flat space misses by 8-18%. The free propagator converges to that of the cone at the same order, and heat diffusion reproduces the $r^6$ measure and the Bessel spectrum of the cone. The maps between neighbouring layers are obtained in closed form from the polar decomposition of the second-quantized Schwinger-boson lift, using a known operator identity, and coincide with the Kov\'a\v{c}ik-Tekel coefficient-copying prescription. For $CP^1$ the construction reduces, away from the outer boundary, to the Kov\'a\v{c}ik-Tekel fuzzy onion. Modes along the twistor fibre are exactly degenerate with the harmonics on $S^4$.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a seven‑dimensional quantum space from concentric fuzzy CP^3 layers and shows that its continuum limit is the metric cone over CP^3 rather than flat R^7, with the Laplacian spectrum converging to that of the cone at second order. The analysis includes explicit maps between layers via Schwinger‑boson techniques and demonstrates exact degeneracy of twistor‑fiber modes with S^4 harmonics, offering a new geometric test for non‑commutative spaces.

papers.title: Supersymmetric Observables from Surface Defect Anomalies in 4d and 6d SCFTs
papers.authors: Zi-Xiao Huang, Ma-Ke Yuan, Yang Zhou
papers.abstract: We study the contributions of half-BPS surface defects to supersymmetric Casimir energy and the universal logarithmic term of supersymmetric R\'enyi entropy in four- and six-dimensional SCFTs. Using equivariant integration of defect anomaly polynomials and its extension to supersymmetric R\'enyi backgrounds, we obtain closed expressions for these observables in terms of defect 't Hooft anomalies. For Gukov--Witten defects preserving transverse rotations in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang--Mills theories, both observables depend on a single R-symmetry anomaly. For $\mathcal{N} = (0, 4)$ defects in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (1, 0)$ theories, additional terms arise from the gravitational anomaly. We provide complementary checks using chiral algebras, five-dimensional localization, and holographic probe branes at large $N$, while localized chiral fermions reproduce the gravitational-anomaly contributions. The framework also recovers Wilson-surface results in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (2, 0)$ theories.
papers.summary: This work derives closed-form expressions for supersymmetric Casimir energy and the universal logarithmic term of supersymmetric Rényi entropy for half-BPS surface defects in 4d and 6d SCFTs, expressing them in terms of defect ’t Hooft anomalies via equivariant integration of anomaly polynomials. The authors verify their results with chiral algebra techniques, 5d localization, holographic probe branes at large N, and localized chiral fermions, extending the framework to include Gukov–Witten defects and Wilson surfaces.

papers.title: Geometry and holography of $\mathrm{AdS}_2\times\mathrm{S}^2$: towards the field theory dual
papers.abstract: We take a first step in identifying the superconformal quantum mechanics dual to supersymmetric AdS$_2\times$S$^2$ solutions. We focus on the Type IIB solutions of the form AdS$_2\times$S$^2\times$CY$_2\times\Sigma$ that preserve eight supercharges, with $\Sigma$ a two-dimensional space parametrised by $(x_1,x_2)$, and read off their brane content, a D1-D5-NS5 intersection with D3 and D7 flavour branes.
