We propose that their dual $\mathcal{N}=4$ quantum mechanics is organised over a two-dimensional lattice of cells in $\Sigma$. Namely, it consists of copies of the linear quiver along $x_1$ dual to the U(1)-invariant solutions of the class, one for each interval along $x_2$, with ranks given by the D1 and D5 charges of the corresponding cell. Its central charge agrees with the holographic one at leading order. We show that the family of SL$(2,\mathbb{R})$ non-Abelian T-duals of the AdS$_3\times$S$^2\times$CY$_2$ solutions of massive Type IIA supergravity, constructed in previous work, belongs to this class, as does the SL$(2,\mathbb{R})\times$SU$(2)$ non-Abelian T-dual of AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times$CY$_2$, and work both out in detail. For both we propose global completions that introduce additional D3 and D7 branes. Along $x_2$ we interpret the fundamental strings stretched between the colour branes and the additional D3 and D7 branes as baryon vertices. Finally, we extend this proposal from the non-Abelian T-duals to the solutions of the class whose defining functions factorise in $x_1$ and $x_2$, including those in which the AdS$_2$ and S$^2$ factors have the same warp factor.
papers.summary: The paper constructs Type IIB AdS$_2	imes$S$^2$ solutions with eight supercharges, identifies their D-brane intersection content, and proposes an $mathcal N=4$ quantum mechanics dual built from a two-dimensional lattice of linear quivers whose ranks are set by D1/D5 charges. The authors check the central charge against holography, analyze non-Abelian T-dual families, and suggest global completions with extra D3/D7 branes, interpreting fundamental strings as baryon vertices.

papers.title: Giant Graviton Expansions from Symmetric Functions and Free Fermions
papers.abstract: Giant graviton expansions express finite-rank corrections to supersymmetric indices in terms of indices for wrapped D3-branes. We give detailed algebraic proofs of two previously proposed relations for four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ $U(N)$ super-Yang--Mills theory. The first is the Gaiotto--Lee single-sum expansion of the full superconformal index, proved by Hall--Littlewood orthogonality and an elementary calculation of operator traces. The second is the symmetric double-sum expansion of the flavored Schur index, proved by factorizing its exact free-fermion mode product. We specify the analytic continuation of the brane indices and justify the sums coefficient by coefficient. The two proofs apply to different expansion prescriptions and do not establish the full three-species expansion of Imamura. We discuss the additional physical and mathematical questions raised by that expansion and by the modular properties of the Schur index.
papers.summary: This paper proves two conjectured expansions of the four‑dimensional $mathcal N=4$ super‑Yang–Mills superconformal index in terms of giant graviton (wrapped D3‑brane) contributions, using Hall–Littlewood orthogonality for the Gaiotto–Lee single‑sum and a free‑fermion factorization for the symmetric double‑sum of the flavored Schur index. The results clarify the analytic continuation of brane indices and illuminate the modular structure of the Schur index, but do not resolve the full three‑species expansion proposed by Imamura.

papers.title: Black Strings and Black Holes: Worldsheet Spectra and Near-Extremal Limits
papers.abstract: We study aspects of the Euclidean partition function of the $\frac{SL(2,\mathbb R)\times U(1)}{U(1)}$ gauged WZW model. The target space geometry is either a smooth horizonless geometry with a linear-dilaton asymptotic region, or the Horne--Horowitz black string, depending on which circles we unwind as the time-direction. We first study the worldsheet spectrum and obtain the character decomposition via the holonomy integrals. Next, we obtain the spacetime spectrum of the horizonless geometry by directly performing the unfolded modular integrals, and recover the Maldacena-Ooguri-Son spectrum in the ungauged limit. When the chirally charged three-dimensional black string is dimensionally reduced, the target space is instead a two-dimensional charged black hole. We study the near extremal regime of the black hole and black string. For the two dimensional black hole, we propose two candidate towers of states that produce the expected $\frac{3}{2}\log T$ of the AdS$_2$ throat from the worldsheet discrete series representation. These towers appear only below the temperature at which the full amplitude becomes divergent. We comment on the contribution of these states in the near-extremal limit of the full partition function.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes the Euclidean partition function of the SL(2,R)×U(1)/U(1) gauged WZW model, deriving the worldsheet spectrum and its character decomposition, and then computes the spacetime spectrum for both horizonless geometries and the Horne–Horowitz black string, recovering known results in the ungauged limit. It further studies the near‑extremal regime of the resulting two‑dimensional charged black hole, proposing discrete‑series towers that reproduce the expected 3/2 log T entropy contribution from the AdS₂ throat before the full amplitude diverges.

papers.title: Carrollian Yang-Mills theories in the homogeneous temporal gauge
papers.abstract: We quantize, in the homogeneous temporal gauge, both the electric and the magnetic Carrollian Yang-Mills theories with SU(N) gauge symmetry in the fundamental representation. We use the BRST method implemented in the path integral. We show that in the first case all the interaction vertices vanish, thus, giving a free theory. In the magnetic case, there are no loop contributions to the Green functions of the elementary fields --i.e., Green functions not involving composite operators-- and the only connected parts of such Green functions with a dependence on the coupling constant are the tree level contributions to the three and four point functions of the field $\xi_i$. We also show that in the magnetic case the Green functions involving only Wilson loops are trivial and not so in the electric case.
papers.summary: The paper quantizes Carrollian Yang–Mills theories in a homogeneous temporal gauge, finding that the electric sector is free while the magnetic sector yields only tree‑level three‑ and four‑point interactions for the field η_i and trivial Wilson‑loop correlators. It demonstrates that loop corrections vanish for elementary Green functions in the magnetic case, highlighting a stark contrast between the two Carrollian limits.

papers.title: Imaginary HTEE: Probing Criticality and Coherence
papers.authors: M. Ali-Akbari, M. M. Daryaei Goki
papers.abstract: We study the imaginary part of the holographic timelike entanglement entropy (HTEE) in a charged asymptotically AdS$_5$ black-hole background whose dual field theory exhibits a critical point in the presence of a chemical potential $\mu$ and temperature $T$. Identifying the imaginary part of the HTEE with the imaginary part of the pseudoentropy, we derive an analytical expression for this quantity and investigate its behavior on the stable and unstable thermodynamic branches. We find that the imaginary HTEE vanishes in the uncharged limit and is induced entirely by a nonzero chemical potential, signaling the emergence of quantum coherence between the initial and final states. As the dimensionless ratio $\mu/T$ approaches its critical value, we obtain an inverse-square-root divergence in the derivative of the imaginary HTEE and extract the critical exponent $\theta_I = 1/2$ analytically. We further show that the same exponent governs the temperature response at fixed chemical potential. Our results establish the imaginary part of the HTEE as a non-local quantum-information probe of criticality in strongly coupled systems, and they imply that the initial and final states become maximally coherent at the critical point.
papers.summary: The authors compute the imaginary part of holographic timelike entanglement entropy in a charged AdS$_5$ black hole, linking it to pseudoentropy and quantum coherence. They find a universal critical exponent $	heta_I=1/2$ for the divergence of its derivative near the chemical‑potential‑driven critical point, suggesting the imaginary HTEE as a non‑local probe of criticality.

papers.title: Late-time electric screening in dS from EAdS loops
papers.authors: Ernesto Bianchi, Sacha Ployet, Charlotte Sleight, Massimo Taronna
papers.abstract: We compute the one-loop gauge-field two-point functions analytically in scalar QED on dS$_{d+1}$ for general dimension and scalar mass, using the EAdS reformulation of the in-in formalism arXiv:2007.09993. The Dirichlet EAdS gauge field acquires a Schwinger-type mass, with its longitudinal mode supplied by a composite of charged scalars obeying opposite boundary conditions, while the Neumann mode remains protected by gauge invariance. In dS, the Dirichlet correction induces an anomalous dimension $\gamma_J$ for the boundary current and modifies the late-time falloff of the electric field. This bulk calculation reproduces the boundary multiplet-recombination result of arXiv:2509.18888. Summing over the in-in contour branches gives the retarded dS bubble kernel, making direct contact with the Bros-Moschella framework. We establish a spectral Cutkosky rule that expresses the discontinuity of this kernel across the principal-series cut in the Casimir plane in terms of a two-particle cut, with both internal scalar lines placed on shell. Although the full bubble coefficient involves a ${}_7F_6$ hypergeometric function, the cut collapses to a closed product of Gamma functions and determines the complete non-local part of the kernel through a dispersion relation. Analytic continuation of the same cut reproduces the complete one-loop result for $\gamma_J$. In the complex Casimir plane, the loop-corrected Dirichlet photon appears as a pole on the second sheet and is therefore naturally interpreted as a dS resonance, or quasinormal mode, whose frequency is shifted at one loop.
papers.summary: The paper analytically computes one-loop gauge-field two-point functions in scalar QED on de Sitter space using an EAdS reformulation of the in-in formalism, revealing a Schwinger-type mass for Dirichlet gauge fields and a nontrivial anomalous dimension for the boundary current. It further establishes a spectral Cutkosky rule, connects the result to a dispersion relation, and interprets the loop-corrected photon as a de Sitter resonance (quasinormal mode).

papers.title: Computation of unknotting numbers: which knot breaks the Bernhard-Jablan Conjecture
papers.abstract: We determine $2,540$ unknotting numbers of prime knots with at most $13$ crossings, that are unknown in the KnotInfo snapshot of 9 September 2026. The lower-bound calculations use Heegaard Floer correction-term obstructions and Greene's spanning-tree model. We also give explicit crossing-change constructions for upper bounds. For $959$ alternating knots with range $[2,3]$, we verify that no crossing change in a minimal diagram gives a knot of unknotting number one. We determine the unknotting numbers of all four knots in Brittenham and Hermiller's construction and thereby identify 13n3370 as an explicit counterexample to the original Bernhard-Jablan conjecture.
papers.summary: This paper computes unknotting numbers for many prime knots up to 13 crossings, using Heegaard Floer correction terms and spanning-tree models, and provides explicit crossing-change constructions. It also identifies a counterexample to the Bernhard-Jablan conjecture by analyzing a specific knot.

papers.title: Black hole sensitivity in Einstein--aether theory
papers.authors: Morgan Kidnew, Andrew Kovachik, Sergey Sibiryakov
papers.abstract: We numerically find the solutions for slowly moving Schwarzschild black holes in Einstein--aether theory. We use these solutions to compute the sensitivity parameter which describes the coupling of the black hole to the aether field within point-particle effective theory. A simple analytic approximation for the dependence of the sensitivity on the Einstein--aether parameters is derived.
papers.summary: The authors numerically construct slowly moving Schwarzschild black hole solutions in Einstein–aether theory and use them to compute the sensitivity parameter that quantifies how the black hole couples to the aether field. They also provide a simple analytic approximation for how this sensitivity depends on the theory’s coupling constants.

papers.title: A Gauge-Inspired Coupled Fokker--Planck System for Multistate Stochastic Dynamics: Formalism and 1-D Numerical Implementation
papers.authors: Francesco Pio De Cosmo, Gianluca Di Natale, Leandro Cieri
papers.abstract: Extending the Fokker--Planck equation to a coupled system of equations through non-Abelian symmetry groups offers a powerful theoretical framework for coupled multi-state stochastic systems. However, translating this abstract gauge field formulation into viable numerical predictions remains an unaddressed challenge. Motivated by our previous work on ice crystal habit evolution, in this work we bridge this gap by presenting the first numerical solver for an SU(2) gauge-coupled Fokker--Planck system in (1+1) dimensions. Using an operator-splitting scheme combined with a non-oscillatory advection solver, our algorithm strictly ensures probability conservation, non-negativity, and numerical stability. We demonstrate that non-Abelian gauge coupling acts as a cross-reactive feedback loop that fundamentally alters system dynamics, driving continuous probability exchange between states, suppressing localised density peaks, and forcing long-time spatial delocalisation. Validated across linear and quadratic coupling regimes up to strong interactions (g <= 1.0), this work establishes the foundational computational infrastructure needed to integrate complex multi-state physics. Overall, while our approach provides a key step toward improving ice cloud representation in atmospheric and climate models, the underlying physical framework and computational engine remain fundamentally general and multidisciplinary, offering a versatile paradigm for any domain requiring coupled multi-state stochastic equations.
papers.summary: The authors develop a numerical solver for an SU(2)-coupled Fokker–Planck system in (1+1) dimensions, ensuring probability conservation and stability via operator splitting and non‑oscillatory advection. They show that non‑Abelian gauge coupling induces continuous probability exchange, suppresses density peaks, and drives spatial delocalisation, with potential applications to ice cloud modeling.

papers.title: The Future of AI-assisted Physics: Discovering, Verifying and Organizing Results via Formalization
papers.authors: Sven Krippendorf, Leopoldo Sarra, Joseph Tooby-Smith
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in AI have opened a new era for physics, enabling unprecedented capabilities in research and discovery. However, these advances also bring challenges in verifying, trusting, and reusing the results they so rapidly produce. Formalization is a necessary part of the solution to these challenges. In this paper, as well as giving an overview of the role of AI and formalization in physics, we make the case that: (1) formalization is an essential layer for AI-driven discoveries in both computational and theoretical physics; (2) AI is lowering the barrier to, and increasing the efficiency of, formalization in physics, though it remains weaker at choosing definitions and designing libraries than at writing proofs; (3) the speed AI brings to formalization in physics currently comes at the cost of trust, credit, and community; (4) shared, community-reviewed formal libraries such as Physlib should be central in making progress in this field, both as a trusted, reusable foundation for physics results and as the environment in which AI systems can reason about physics; (5) formalizing physics raises challenges beyond those in mathematics, most importantly that a checked proof does not establish that its definitions faithfully capture the intended physics. We also give our perspectives on near-term and long-term directions in these areas.
papers.summary: The paper argues that formalization is essential for AI-driven physics, outlining how AI can accelerate but also challenge trust and credit. It proposes community libraries like Physlib to serve as a shared foundation for verified results.

papers.title: Ultralight scalars and invisible gravitons
papers.abstract: Unless the tensor to scalar ratio is small enough, the non-adiabatic mode associated with the ultralight bosons may be dangerously comparable with the adiabatic spectrum of curvature inhomogeneities. We point out here that this statement depends on the timeline of the post-inflationary expansion rate. Provided the decelerated evolution is slower than radiation for a sufficiently long period, the relative weight of the non-adiabatic and adiabatic components does not conflict with the direct constraints coming from the large-scale observations. Conversely the presence of ultralight bosons excludes the presence of long stages expanding faster than radiation. The synthesis of the light nuclei and the spectrum of the relic gravitons at high frequencies set the relevant constraints on the duration of the decelerated stages, on the delayed dominance of radiation and on the mass range of the ultralight scalars.
papers.summary: The paper examines how ultralight scalar fields can generate non‑adiabatic perturbations that compete with the adiabatic curvature spectrum, depending on the post‑inflationary expansion history. It shows that a prolonged sub‑radiation deceleration can suppress the non‑adiabatic mode, while faster expansion phases are ruled out by BBN and high‑frequency graviton bounds.

papers.title: Categorifying Quantum Spin Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a homotopical framework for understanding the space of quantum spin systems based on topological $n$-nets, which assign associative unital algebras to local regions in an $n$-dimensional space in a manner that captures the locality structure of the underlying lattice theories. The net-theoretic perspective admits a natural categorification, in which the category of topological $n$-nets carries the structure of a higher Morita category. Moreover, the nets of greatest physical interest form a Karoubi-complete subcategory that shares many of the characteristic structural features of the category of finite TQFTs. Our main result identifies the group of locality-preserving symmetries of (3+1)-dimensional quantum spin systems (i.e. quantum cellular automata modulo stabilization, finite-depth quantum circuits, and translations) with the full Witt group of nondegenerate braided fusion categories, thereby answering a question posed by Haah.
papers.summary: This paper develops a homotopical framework for quantum spin systems using topological n‑nets and shows that the category of such nets forms a higher Morita category. The authors prove that the group of locality‑preserving symmetries in 3+1 dimensions is isomorphic to the Witt group of nondegenerate braided fusion categories, resolving a question by Haah.

papers.title: A Witten effect for global monopoles
papers.abstract: Global monopoles can carry electric charge even when the scalar field that forms them is neutral. We show that a CP-odd operator in the Goldstone effective theory, typically discarded as a total derivative, gives them an electric charge $Q=-Cn$, with $C$ its Wilson coefficient and $n$ the winding number. This is a Witten effect on a global defect, generated by a mixed $\theta$-term between electromagnetism and a composite connection built from the Goldstone fields. The same group theory condition that allows the operator also guarantees the existence of monopoles. We also give a fermionic UV completion and determine the coefficient by matching the Goldstone-Wilczek current.
papers.summary: This paper shows that global monopoles can acquire electric charge via a CP‑odd operator in the Goldstone effective theory, effectively a Witten effect on a global defect mediated by a mixed θ‑term between electromagnetism and a composite Goldstone connection. The authors also construct a fermionic UV completion and match the Wilson coefficient to the Goldstone‑Wilczek current.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event: A Minimal $U(1)_B$ Dark Sector and Its Experimental Tests
papers.abstract: The $248$ keV nuclear-recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation, in which scattering converts the DM particle into a slightly heavier state. We provide a comprehensive study of this interpretation in an anomaly-free model of gauged baryon number, where a new vector boson, $Z_B$, mediates interactions between DM and quarks. Breaking the baryonic gauge symmetry generates the new particle masses and a small splitting between two DM states, while a residual symmetry keeps the lighter state stable. We identify regions compatible with the LZ candidate, the observed DM abundance, and current ATLAS and CMS dijet constraints. Within the scanned domain, these regions span DM masses $m_\chi\simeq0.19$-$4.5$ TeV, mediator masses $M_{Z_B}\simeq0.05$-$5.0$ TeV, and gauge couplings $g_B\simeq0.004$-$0.74$, with correlated values of these parameters. A representative thermal solution has $m_\chi=1$ TeV, $M_{Z_B}=1.44$ TeV, $g_B\simeq0.228$, and a mass splitting of $300$ keV. A small electroweak mixing allows the heavier DM state to decay rapidly, suppressing unwanted signals from its surviving population. This interpretation can be tested through complementary measurements: additional LZ and XENONnT data can establish whether the high-energy recoil signal persists, ATLAS and CMS Run-3 dijet searches can probe the mediator mass and coupling, and a dedicated IceCube analysis of four-quark final states can test DM capture and annihilation in the Sun. Together, these measurements can test complementary parts of the surviving region and assess whether the LZ candidate is consistent with this interpretation.
papers.summary: The paper proposes an inelastic dark matter model with a gauged baryon number U(1)_B to explain the 248 keV recoil event seen by LZ. It explores parameter space consistent with relic density, collider dijet limits, and suggests future tests via LZ, XENONnT, and IceCube.

papers.title: Gauss-Manin Connection in Disguise: Holomorphic Anomaly Equations and Higher Genus Real Gromov-Witten Invariants
papers.abstract: We construct an algebraic framework for the extended holomorphic anomaly equations following ideas of Alim, Movasati, Scheidegger and Yau. We choose the quintic threefold as our main model and use this framework to solve the equations and fix the ambiguity up to genus 5. We obtain predictions for real Gromov-Witten invariants, or, equivalently, real Gopakumar-Vafa invariants that are integers and agree with their complex counterparts modulo 2. In the end, we discuss how the framework could be extended and compute the same predictions for the bicubic up to genus 9.
papers.summary: This work develops an algebraic approach to solve extended holomorphic anomaly equations for the quintic threefold, determining real Gromov-Witten invariants up to genus five and matching them with complex counterparts modulo two. The authors also extend the method to the bicubic model, obtaining predictions up to genus nine.

papers.title: Non-Stationary Wormholes and Matter Source Reconstruction in General Relativity
papers.authors: Geov\'a Alencar, Tiago Crispim, Roberta D\'arlla, Ricardo Landim
papers.abstract: We investigate non-stationary wormhole geometries in General Relativity embedded in evolving cosmological backgrounds. We employ a Simpson-Visser-like regularization of the temporal coordinate of the $(n+1)$-dimensional FLRW metric, together with a homogeneous Cuscuton field, to construct cosmological backgrounds in which the scale factor remains finite and non-zero at the would-be initial singularity. We then consider two specific dynamical wormhole geometries: the four-dimensional defect wormhole and the topologically charged Perry-Mann type wormhole. We show that the former can be supported by a canonical scalar field with vanishing potential, while the latter requires a mimetic matter sector to support its spatial structure, with the Cuscuton governing the cosmological evolution in both cases. We subsequently generalize the analysis to a separable non-stationary spacetime and derive a scaling condition that strongly constrains the admissible matter sources. In particular, for minimally coupled scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics fields, this condition removes the functional freedom available in static reconstruction schemes. We show that, within this framework, regular, asymptotically flat wormhole geometries cannot be obtained while simultaneously satisfying the required smoothness and reflection symmetry conditions. Our results illustrate both the possibility of constructing specific non-stationary wormholes in regular cosmological backgrounds and the restrictions that arise when attempting to generalize such constructions to arbitrary spatial geometries.
papers.summary: The paper constructs non‑stationary wormhole solutions in General Relativity by embedding them in regular cosmological backgrounds using a Cuscuton field and a Simpson‑Visser‑like time regularization. It then derives scaling constraints that rule out regular, asymptotically flat wormholes with smoothness and reflection symmetry for minimally coupled scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics sources.

papers.title: Lifts of symmetries to minimal nondegenerate extensions are unique up to fermion attachment
papers.abstract: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. Our results require neither unitarity nor a ribbon structure. We illustrate the lifting ambiguity in the Laughlin state, the $SO(3)_3$ theory and the Ising topological order.
papers.summary: The paper proves that for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category, any symmetry of the underlying fermionic topological order lifts uniquely to its minimal nondegenerate extension up to attaching the fermion, with exactly two lift classes distinguished by fermionic self‑braiding. This result is established via tensor‑categorical methods, extending graph algebras to Lagrangian algebras, and applies to models such as the Laughlin state, SO(3)_3, and the Ising topological order.

papers.title: Quantum Energy Inequalities with a twist: rotating frames along stationary worldlines
papers.authors: Christopher J. Fewster, Daniel Lomax Ford
papers.abstract: The energy densities of the quantised scalar and electromagnetic fields need not be positive, but their averages along timelike worldlines are constrained by Quantum Energy Inequalities (QEIs) that hold in flat and curved spacetimes for arbitrary Hadamard quantum field states. However the general QEI bound is not easy to compute in closed form. Here, we compute closed form expressions for the massless scalar and electromagnetic fields along stationary worldlines in Minkowski spacetime. These worldlines are solutions to the four-dimensional Frenet-Serret equations with constant curvature invariants and include inertial, uniformly linearly accelerated, and uniformly rotating worldlines as special cases. The QEI bound depends on a choice of tetrad along the worldline, and we compute it for any tetrad with constant angular velocity relative to the Frenet-Serret tetrad. Optimising over the angular velocity, we show that the tightest electromagnetic QEI bound occurs when the tetrad is invariant under Fermi-Walker tetrads. Surprisingly, the Fermi-Walker tetrad does not produce the tightest QEI bound for massless scalar fields, and we investigate the optimal bound both analytically and numerically. Our results and methodology significantly improve on those in [CJ Fewster & J Thompson, Class. Quantum Grav. 40 (2023) 175008], in which only Frenet-Serret tetrads were considered for massless scalar fields.
papers.summary: The authors derive closed‑form quantum energy inequalities for massless scalar and electromagnetic fields along any stationary worldline in Minkowski space, including inertial, uniformly accelerated and uniformly rotating trajectories. They show that the tightest bounds are obtained by tetrads that are Fermi‑Walker invariant for the electromagnetic case, while for the scalar field a different optimal tetrad is required, revealing a subtle dependence on the observer’s rotation.

papers.title: Cosmology & Astrophysics of the Dark Dimension with Bulk Majorana Neutrinos
papers.abstract: Recently, the possibility of having sterile Majorana neutrinos charged under $B-L$ gauge symmetry in the bulk of the dark dimension has been explored. We point out a cosmological restriction on the Majorana mass of bulk neutrinos leading to mass $\gtrsim 100~{\rm GeV}$. This avoids the over-production of Kaluza-Klein neutrino towers in the early universe thus resolving the cosmological neutrino catastrophe of extra dimension scenarios. If the mass of the bulk neutrino is at the lower end of this bound, it can potentially also explain the recently observed Fermi halo excess on gamma rays through the evaporation of long-lived 5d (i.e. dark) black holes through Hawking radiation to bulk neutrinos, which promptly decay into standard model particles.
papers.summary: The paper investigates constraints on bulk Majorana neutrinos in a dark extra dimension, showing that a mass above ~100 GeV is required to avoid overproducing KK towers in the early universe, thereby resolving the cosmological neutrino catastrophe. It further proposes that near‑threshold bulk neutrinos could explain the Fermi gamma‑ray halo excess via Hawking evaporation of long‑lived 5‑dimensional black holes into neutrinos that decay to SM particles.

papers.title: Primordial Graviton Entanglement in Quasicrystalline Inflation
papers.abstract: We study the entanglement structure of gravitons in quasicrystalline inflation. Both parity-even and parity-odd interactions generate graviton pairs with nonzero total momentum. For opposite-helicity pairs with identical momenta, the parity-even contribution can be nonzero, whereas the parity-odd contribution vanishes. The transition from inflation to radiation domination produces additional conventional two-mode squeezing. We derive the resulting normal and anomalous covariances. The initially nonzero reciprocal blocks of the full field-momentum covariance remain nonzero under homogeneous evolution, although individual components can vanish. We show that this homogeneous, helicity-preserving evolution acts unitarily within each helicity sector and therefore preserves the entanglement between the complete right- and left-helicity sectors. Nevertheless, it can eliminate entanglement in the reduced state of a co-propagating pair. We illustrate this distinction using a solvable four-mode model.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes the entanglement of graviton pairs produced during quasicrystalline inflation, focusing on parity‑even and parity‑odd interactions and their impact on two‑mode squeezing and covariance matrices. It demonstrates that while helicity‑preserving homogeneous evolution preserves total entanglement, it can erase entanglement in reduced co‑propagating pairs, illustrated via a solvable four‑mode model.

papers.title: Valley-resolved high harmonics probe symmetry breaking beyond the Dirac cone
papers.authors: Pablo Pais, Alfredo Iorio, Marcelo F. Ciappina
papers.abstract: Low-energy electrons in graphene obey an emergent, rotationally invariant Dirac equation, while the honeycomb lattice enters only through higher-order, symmetry-breaking corrections, the leading one being trigonal warping. This provides a unique solid-state arena to address a cornerstone challenge in quantum gravity: how to detect ultraviolet symmetry-breaking granular corrections, suppressed by a fundamental scale, atop an emergent infrared relativistic continuum. We show that intense counter-rotating $\omega$-$2\omega$ fields and valley-resolved high-harmonic generation (HHG) provide such a probe. Within a family of models that interpolates continuously between the isotropic Dirac cone and nearest-neighbour graphene at fixed Fermi velocity, the valley contrast of the harmonic yield vanishes identically in the symmetric theory, grows linearly with the warping coupling, and its valley-even counterpart appears only at second order, as expected from effective-field-theory power counting. The stronger the laser, the farther it drives electrons from the Dirac points, so the laser intensity plays the role of the collision energy. For the fourth harmonic, the leading warping correction alone accounts for the valley contrast of real graphene up to fundamental intensities of about $10^{11}$ W/cm$^2$, below the damage threshold of monolayer graphene, whereas the fifth harmonic already reveals higher-order lattice corrections at intensities around $10^{10}$ W/cm$^2$. The two harmonics, which rotate in opposite directions, are emitted by opposite valleys. Valley-resolved harmonics are far more sensitive than the residual valley populations, making them a practical detector of lattice-scale physics hidden beneath an emergent Dirac theory.
papers.summary: This work demonstrates that valley-resolved high-harmonic generation in graphene can serve as a sensitive probe of lattice-scale symmetry-breaking corrections to the emergent Dirac continuum, with the valley contrast scaling linearly with trigonal warping. By tuning the intensity of counter-rotating ω–2ω laser fields, the authors show that the fourth harmonic captures first-order warping effects while the fifth harmonic reveals higher-order lattice corrections, offering a practical experimental window into ultraviolet physics hidden beneath the Dirac theory.

papers.title: Modular $S_4$ Inverse Seesaw at the LZ High-Recoil Frontier
papers.authors: Waqas Ahmed, Vasileios Basiouris, George K. Leontaris
papers.abstract: The extension of the LUX--ZEPLIN nuclear-recoil analysis to approximately $270\,\mathrm{keV}$ probes a qualitatively new dark-matter regime in which endothermic scattering can suppress conventional low-energy recoils and concentrate the surviving spectrum near the Galactic high-velocity tail. We construct a modular-$S_4$ realization in which a minimal $2N_R+2S$ inverse seesaw accounts for lepton flavor, while a separate pair of Standard-Model-singlet fermions forms the pseudo-Dirac state relevant for high-recoil xenon scattering. The sectors share a common complex modulus $\tau$, so the modular forms selected by charged-lepton and neutrino data also enter the operators generating the dark Dirac mass and Majorana splitting. Our scan yields $181447$ lepton-sector solutions satisfying $\chi^2_{\ell+\nu}<30$, distributed among several disconnected modular regions, and predicts one effectively massless light neutrino at leading order. Restoring the physical scales allows TeV-scale heavy quasi-Dirac neutral fermions with small non-unitarity. We subsequently scan $2\times10^6$ dark-sector points only over flavor-accepted values of $\tau$ and identify common-modulus solutions in the LZ-oriented region $300\,\mathrm{GeV}\le m_\chi\le2\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and $300\,\mathrm{keV}\le\delta\le400\,\mathrm{keV}$. An exploratory two-bin Poisson likelihood, including endothermic xenon kinematics, the Helm form factor, Standard-Halo-Model velocities, Gaussian energy smearing, and profiling over the signal normalization, gives a best grid point at $(m_\chi,\delta)\simeq(1.847\,\mathrm{TeV},371.5\,\mathrm{keV})$, close to the terrestrial inelastic kinematic ceiling. The construction provides a direct link between modular lepton flavor, TeV-scale inverse-seesaw dynamics, and high-recoil inelastic dark matter.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a modular S4-based inverse seesaw model that links lepton flavor structure to a TeV-scale pseudo-Dirac dark matter candidate, whose endothermic scattering is probed by the LZ experiment up to 270 keV. It performs extensive scans over the common modulus τ to identify parameter points that satisfy neutrino data and yield a dark matter mass in the 300 GeV–2 TeV range with a mass splitting of 300–400 keV, achieving a best-fit point near the kinematic ceiling.

papers.title: Dynamical chiral symmetry breaking in rotating QED$_3$: critical flavor number and the occupation-reweighting channel
papers.abstract: We study dynamical chiral symmetry breaking in $(2{+}1)$-dimensional QED on a rigidly rotating disc, $\Omega R<1$, within the rainbow Schwinger--Dyson framework. At zero temperature the rotation response of the condensate vanishes identically, so $N_c^{\rm SD}(\Omega,T{=}0)=N_c^{\rm SD}(0)=2.60\pm0.01$ (using three operational definitions). At finite temperature, rotation suppresses the condensate through a dominant occupation-reweighting channel, $\hat{\kappa}_{\rm occ}=-1.55$, accounting for $\ge 99.995\%$ of the linearized total response at the reference parameters, with self-consistent feedback amplifying it by $26.5$. The screening channel is reported at fixed regularization, $\hat{\kappa}_{\rm scr}(\varepsilon = 0.01)=-0.97$; its $\varepsilon \to 0$ behavior is logarithmically divergent. The crossover flavor $N^{*}(\Omega)$ falls monotonically at fixed temperature (a corollary). The critical flavor number is unchanged by rotation at $T=0$ (theorem). Together these results set the finite-temperature reference for the model.
papers.summary: The study investigates dynamical chiral symmetry breaking in rotating (2+1)-dimensional QED using a rainbow Schwinger–Dyson approach, finding that the critical flavor number remains unchanged by rotation at zero temperature and that at finite temperature rotation suppresses the condensate mainly via an occupation‑reweighting channel.

papers.title: Axionic Casimir Torque
papers.abstract: In the canonical Casimir effect, the quantum vacuum is isotropic, and the minimization of vacuum energy drives only a linear attractive force between the plates. However, the introduction of an axion gradient breaks this rotational symmetry. It can be demonstrated that these asymmetric zero-point fluctuations exert a macroscopic mechanical twist on the plates proportional to $\vec{b}^2 \sin (2\vartheta)$ where $\vec{b}$ is the spatial axion gradient and $\vartheta$ is the angle between the axion gradient and the normal to the plates.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that an axion gradient breaks rotational symmetry in vacuum fluctuations, producing a macroscopic torque between parallel plates proportional to $vec{b}^2sin(2vartheta)$. This extends the conventional Casimir effect by linking axion physics to observable mechanical forces.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium framework for first-order phase transitions
papers.abstract: The first-order phase transition is central to electroweak baryogenesis and gravitational wave generation, yet thermal equilibrium effective potential analyses cannot describe the real-time non-equilibrium dynamics of the phase transition process. We use the Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path formalism of real-time finite-temperature field theory to study these effects. For the $\phi^6$ model, we derive the effective action and the corresponding Langevin equation. We further extend the formalism to the two scalar fields case, obtaining the coupled Langevin equations. These results provide a theoretical framework for the bubble nucleation simulation of the non-equilibrium phase transition process, laying the foundation for reliable predictions of baryogenesis and gravitational wave signals.
papers.summary: This paper develops a real‑time, non‑equilibrium formalism based on the Schwinger–Keldysh closed‑time‑path approach to study first‑order phase transitions, deriving Langevin equations for a φ^6 theory and extending them to coupled two‑scalar systems. The framework is intended to underpin realistic bubble‑nucleation simulations relevant for electroweak baryogenesis and gravitational‑wave predictions.

papers.title: Entanglement and parametric resonance in coupled oscillator systems
papers.abstract: We study a system of two quadratically-coupled harmonic oscillators, prepared respectively in the ground state and in a coherent state. This toy model can describe for instance the dynamics of one mode of a quantum field evolving in a harmonically-oscillating classical background. In such situations, it is well-known that, depending on the background oscillation amplitude and coupling strength, the system may exhibit parametric resonance. Using the Feynman-Vernon influence functional, we analyze the interplay between parametric resonance and quantum entanglement by perturbatively computing the purity of the mixed state resulting from tracing over one of the oscillators. We find a runaway behavior of the quantum entanglement between the two oscillators, as well as a rapid breakdown of the validity of perturbation theory, in regions of parametric instability. This provides a quantitative confirmation of various statements in the literature and is highly relevant to questions pertaining to the validity of the semiclassical approximation in coupled quantum-classical systems.
papers.summary: This paper studies two quadratically coupled harmonic oscillators, one in the ground state and one in a coherent state, and examines how parametric resonance influences their entanglement using the Feynman–Vernon influence functional, finding runaway entanglement and a breakdown of perturbation theory in unstable regimes. The results confirm expectations about the limits of semiclassical approximations in coupled quantum–classical systems.

papers.title: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
papers.authors: St\'ephane Fay, Mikel Artola, Leandros Perivolaropoulos
papers.abstract: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the standard $\Lambda$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR) linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $\eta(z) \equiv D_{\rm L} / [{(1+z)}^2 D_{\rm A}] = \alpha{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon \!\neq\! 0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $\Lambda$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $\Lambda$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $\Omega_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $\eta(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $\eta(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z < 0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $\alpha \simeq 0.942 \pm 0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also map the CDDR violation onto photon-loss and varying-$G$ scenarios, concluding that the cosmological constraints are much weaker than existing constraints on these physical mechanisms.
papers.summary: The paper examines how allowing a tilt in the cosmic distance duality relation can weaken the apparent preference for dynamical dark energy in DESI BAO and supernova data, finding that the effect is robust across datasets and parametrizations. It also quantifies a normalization mismatch under Planck and SH0ES priors and maps the violation to photon‑loss and varying‑G scenarios, concluding the constraints are weaker than existing limits.

papers.title: Conserved-charge diffusion in hot and dense QCD matter
papers.authors: Dushmanta Sahu, Kangkan Goswami, Raghunath Sahoo
papers.abstract: We study the coupled diffusion of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness in hot and dense quark matter using a three-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model with self-consistently generated constituent quark masses. The complete diffusion matrix is evaluated within a relaxation-time kinetic approach, including its diagonal and off-diagonal components. We find that the off-diagonal transport coefficients exhibit distinct temperature and baryon-chemical-potential dependence associated with the flavor-dependent composition of the charge carriers. We further investigate generalized charge diffusivities and mobilities obtained from the corresponding susceptibilities. At finite baryon chemical potential, the baryon and strangeness mobility scales cross, reflecting the different density dependence of their transport coefficients and susceptibilities. The results provide model benchmarks for coupled conserved-charge transport in baryon-rich QCD matter.
papers.summary: The paper computes the full diffusion matrix for baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness in hot, dense quark matter using a three‑flavor NJL model, revealing significant off‑diagonal transport coefficients that vary with temperature and chemical potential. It also extracts generalized diffusivities and mobilities, showing a crossing of baryon and strangeness mobilities at finite chemical potential, thus offering benchmark results for coupled conserved‑charge transport in baryon‑rich QCD.

papers.title: Where is the conformal coupling in Palatini gravity?
papers.abstract: We study the conformal coupling in the torsion-free Palatini formulation with an ordinary scalar kinetic term. Tuning the curvature coupling cannot restore Weyl invariance in a Palatini theory with an ordinary scalar kinetic term because, for an independent and inert connection, the scalar-curvature term is separately Weyl-invariant, and no finite curvature coupling cancels the Weyl variation of the kinetic term. This can be demonstrated by evaluating the energy-momentum trace on the scalar equation of motion and noting that it is explicitly independent of the Palatini coupling. Eliminating the connection, we construct a map between the curvature coupling and the effective coupling for the equivalent metric theory, and demonstrate that the scalar continues to propagate even if the reduced kinetic coefficient vanishes. We also show that it becomes a Weyl compensator with a scale-invariant potential only in the rescaled infinite-coupling limit, which in four dimensions is directly related to Palatini ${\cal R}^2$ gravity. We calculate the running of the couplings at one loop, and we find that the conformal shift in the metric-curvature coupling's beta function generates a metric-curvature coupling on a fixed metric-affine background, whereas the independent-curvature coupling runs homogeneously. Furthermore, we follow an alternate prescription in which the connection is allowed to respond to the scalar fluctuations, which results in a different scalar Hessian and therefore different beta functions. Nonetheless, we find that both prescriptions admit the formal infrared limit $(\xi_{eff},\lambda_{eff})\to(1/6,0)$ through different limits of the original couplings in the case of positive perturbative quartics. Finally, we note that trajectories starting on the positive gravitational branch encounter a vanishing gravitational coefficient at a finite scale before this endpoint.
papers.summary: This paper shows that in torsion‑free Palatini gravity a scalar field cannot be made Weyl invariant by any finite curvature coupling, and that the effective metric coupling is mapped to the Palatini coupling after eliminating the connection. It further computes one‑loop beta functions, revealing that the metric‑curvature coupling runs homogeneously while the independent curvature coupling generates a metric‑curvature term on a fixed background, and that both prescriptions flow to the conformal point in the infrared.

papers.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
papers.authors: Martin Rosenlyst, Vinh Tran, Oliver Zier, Xuejian Shen, Mark Vogelsberger, Thejs Brinckmann, Mads T. Frandsen, Jes\'us Zavala, Frederik Holt Dihver Christensen, Mikkel Theiss Kristensen
papers.abstract: We develop a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), connecting microscopic dark-sector physics to nonlinear structure formation. We systematize particle-physics ingredients of representative SIDM models and map microscopic parameters and interactions onto structure-formation simulation inputs. These include internal-state populations and reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, inelastic and dissipative energy exchange, decay rates and recoil kinematics, and modifications to cosmological initial conditions. The numerical framework builds on the efficient, scalable SIDM infrastructure introduced in our companion work for the moving-mesh code AREPO-2, providing substantial performance gains over AREPO-1. We implement isotropic and anisotropic self-scattering with constant or velocity-dependent cross sections, multi-state and inelastic reactions, and dissipative scattering, complemented by a dedicated dark-matter decay module. For strongly forward-peaked interactions, the anisotropic hybrid SIDM scheme combines frequent small-angle drag-diffusion with explicit rare large-angle scattering, achieving speed-ups of up to $\sim100\times$ relative to fully anisotropic Monte Carlo in the tested configurations. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection experiments, thermalization and uniform-box decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. These tests recover analytical predictions, establish consistency between equivalent numerical treatments, and reproduce published inelastic and dissipative SIDM benchmarks. The resulting modular framework connects dark-sector models to nonlinear astrophysical predictions, enabling exploration of microscopic interactions beyond standard isotropic, elastic SIDM.
papers.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive computational framework linking microscopic self‑interacting dark matter models to large‑scale structure simulations, incorporating velocity‑dependent cross sections, inelastic processes, and decay modules in AREPO‑2. It demonstrates significant performance gains and validates the implementation against analytical benchmarks, enabling detailed studies of dark‑sector physics in cosmological contexts.

papers.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
papers.abstract: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that bound sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band, beam-beam hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming such limitation. Driven by modest jet misalignments ($\theta_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 6^\circ$), co-streaming proton beams collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ - six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in a strictly optically thin regime ($\tau_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary PeV-EeV neutrinos and sub-TeV $\gamma$-rays fall directly within reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.
papers.summary: This paper proposes that sub-parsec binary blazars can act as natural hadronic colliders, achieving center-of-mass energies up to 10^10 GeV, far beyond terrestrial accelerators. It discusses how these systems could probe QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and potential new physics through high-energy neutrino and gamma-ray signatures observable by current detectors.

papers.title: Vanishing Love Numbers of Kerr-Newman Black Holes
papers.authors: Sumanta Chakraborty, Takuya Katagiri, Paolo Pani, Jun-Xi Shi
papers.abstract: Tidal Love numbers characterize the conservative response of compact objects to external perturbations and provide a powerful probe of their nature. While the static Love numbers of Schwarzschild, Kerr, and Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes remarkably vanish, the tidal response of a generic Kerr--Newman black hole has remained unexplored due to the intrinsic coupling between gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations. Exploiting a recent breakthrough in the separability of these perturbations, we analytically determine the static tidal response of the most general stationary black hole in four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For arbitrary multipole order, charge, and spin, we show that the entire matrix of conservative Love numbers vanishes, including the mixed gravito-electromagnetic couplings. We also compute the nonvanishing static dissipative response induced by frame dragging.
papers.summary: The paper analytically shows that all static tidal Love numbers, including mixed gravito-electromagnetic couplings, vanish for Kerr–Newman black holes, extending the known result for Schwarzschild, Kerr, and Reissner–Nordström cases. It also computes the nonzero static dissipative response due to frame dragging.

papers.title: Revisiting Critical Higgs Inflation: Electroweak Couplings, CMB Observables, and Perturbative Unitarity
papers.authors: Sarah R. Geller, Sol Gutierrez-Lara, David I. Kaiser, Thomas Steingasser
papers.abstract: We revisit the scenario of critical Higgs inflation, in which inflation is driven by the Standard Model Higgs boson with parameters chosen close to a critical point, giving rise to an inflection point in its potential. After reviewing this model, we perform a systematic study of its viability centered around three criteria: (1) consistency with electroweak-scale measurements, (2) ability to reproduce the cosmic microwave background (CMB) observables, and (3) sensitivity of the model predictions to unknown UV physics, based on a breakdown of perturbative unitarity. We first show that compliance with electroweak-scale measurements is controlled by the parameters in the Higgs potential at inflationary scales, also updating the literature values. We then demonstrate how for any choice of potential parameters, agreement with the CMB observables can be achieved through the choice of the nonminimal coupling, in both metric and Palatini formulations of gravity. However, we also find that there exist no regions of parameter space, in either the metric or Palatini formulations, in which compliance with all three physical criteria is possible. While this does not exclude the possibility of the Higgs field driving inflation, it means that predictions for any observable are in principle sensitive to the details of the model's UV completion.
papers.summary: The paper revisits critical Higgs inflation, showing that electroweak constraints can be met and CMB observables reproduced by tuning the nonminimal coupling in both metric and Palatini gravity. However, it finds no parameter region that satisfies electroweak consistency, CMB agreement, and perturbative unitarity simultaneously, indicating UV sensitivity of the model.

papers.title: What Do Event Generators Compute? Flux Functionals from Detector Operators
papers.abstract: Every physical prediction of an event generator is a statement about the hadronic fluxes that can be recorded by particle detectors. By contrast, the formal backbone of modern event-generator precision is provided by the unobservable partonic final states of the parton shower, with hadronisation included as a model. We construct the probability distribution of the hadronic fluxes non-perturbatively, directly from detector operators acting on asymptotic hadronic states, and encode it in an event generator source functional. This distribution contains every measurement a detector can make, and is therefore what a generator must compute with precision, including the effects of hadronisation. Restricting the functional to the energy flow yields the parton shower source functional, which is infrared and collinear safe and contains every calorimetric observable, making it a natural object against which to assess parton-shower accuracy. We compute its logarithmic structure at one loop in $e^+e^-$ annihilation, finding it directly sensitive to kinematic recoil and hence to the recoil scheme of a parton shower. The parton shower functional depends on a continuum of low scales, one for each resolved direction, and in a toy model its logarithms cannot be entirely resummed within a factorisation whose evolution derives only from the high-scale physics. Our operator-based formulation opens the door to the study of event-generator-like systems in theories beyond QCD, including conformal theories such as $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory, and thereby offers a new route to non-perturbative insight into event generation.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a non‑perturbative probability distribution for hadronic fluxes directly from detector operators, encoding it as an event‑generator source functional that includes hadronisation effects. It shows that the parton‑shower functional, infrared‑safe and containing all calorimetric observables, can be computed at one loop in $e^+e^-$ annihilation, revealing sensitivity to recoil schemes and highlighting limitations of factorisation in resumming its logarithms.

papers.title: Internal Nucleon Properties and the Equation of State of Ultra-Dense Matter
papers.authors: Bikram Keshari Pradhan, J\'er\^ome Margueron, Guy Chanfray, Hubert Hansen
papers.abstract: The question of the link between the nucleon properties and the equation of state of ultra-dense matter, both being composed of quarks and gluons, is investigated by adopting a soliton model to describe internal nucleon properties and a direct mapping between nucleon and quark matter to obtain the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. We compare $\pi+\omega$ and $\pi+\omega+\rho$ soliton models and analyze the presence of a pressure singularity at the nucleon center due to the $\rho$ field. This singularity impacts the equation of state in ultra-dense matter. Only the pressure derived from the canonical energy-momentum tensor has a singularity, while the Belinfante pseudo-gauge transformation of the energy-momentum tensor generates an internal pressure without a singularity. We then investigate predictions for the equation of state of ultra-dense matter based on different prescriptions for the nucleon pressure. It is shown that none of the prescriptions agree with the thermodynamical pressure defined in uniform matter. The mismatch between any equation of state and the thermodynamical one questions the simplicity of the direct mapping between finite-size nucleon properties and uniform matter as well as the role of the nucleon surface in the internal energy density and the pressure.
papers.summary: This paper investigates how soliton models of the nucleon can be mapped to the equation of state of ultra-dense matter, focusing on pressure singularities arising from the ρ field and the differences between canonical and Belinfante energy-momentum tensors. The authors find that none of the proposed nucleon-pressure prescriptions reproduce the thermodynamic pressure of uniform matter, casting doubt on the direct mapping approach.

papers.title: On quasi-lisse affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories
papers.authors: Drazen Adamovic, Xuanzhong Dai, Kaiwen Sun
papers.abstract: We study certain simple affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-simply-laced simple Lie algebra and $h$ is its Coxeter number. For $L_{-3}(F_4)$, we determine the maximal ideal of $V^{-3}(F_4)$, Zhu's algebra, and the associated variety. We also classify the irreducible highest-weight $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules and determine the characters of its irreducible ordinary modules. The associated variety is $\overline{\mathbb{O}}_{\widetilde A_1}$, and the level $-3$ is totally collapsing for the orbit $\mathbb{O}_{\widetilde A_1}$. The Poisson coinvariants of the $C_2$-algebra of $L_{-3}(F_4)$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}[\ell]/(\ell^5)$, where $\ell$ is induced by the conformal vector. Consequently, the characters of ordinary $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules satisfy a fifth-order modular linear differential equation. We also give modular linear differential equations of orders five and eleven satisfied by the characters of ordinary modules for $L_{-2}(B_3)$ and $L_{-2}(G_2)$ respectively.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes simple affine vertex algebras arising from rank‑one Argyres‑Douglas theories, determining their maximal ideals, Zhu algebras, and associated varieties, and classifying all irreducible highest‑weight modules for the case (L_{-3}(F_4)). It further shows that the characters of ordinary modules satisfy fifth‑order modular linear differential equations, illustrating a deep link between representation theory and modularity.

papers.title: Signature of GW from the Hidden Sector in light of the Recent LZ Event
papers.authors: Sujit Kumar Sahoo, Narendra Sahu, Vicky Singh Thounaojam
papers.abstract: The LZ collaboration has recently reported a single nuclear-recoil event at $E_R=248\pm23_\text{stat}\pm23_\text{sys}$ keV, observed in a 2.84 tonne-year exposure with a local significance of $3.4\sigma$, pointing towards an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation. We explain this event within a gauged $U(1)_X$ hidden-sector model, spontaneously broken by a singlet scalar whose vacuum expectation value (VEV) gives rise to: \textit{(i)} gauge boson mass, \textit{(ii)} a small Majorana mass for the vector-like singlet fermion, the DM candidate, charged under the new symmetry, which splits the fermion into two pseudo-Dirac states (mass splitting proportional to the scalar VEV) thus resulting in a purely off-diagonal vector current, \textit{(iii)} the frequency and the amplitude of the GW signal arising from the hidden sector symmetry breaking via first-order phase transition (FOPT). The symmetry-breaking scale thus provides a multi-messenger probe connecting terrestrial direct-detection kinematics at the LZ and early-universe FOPT thermodynamics while obtaining thermal DM relic abundance. We delineate the viable parameter space compatible with the LZ event, correct relic density, and detectable GW signals in the low frequency regimes at future interferometers like $\mu {\rm ARES}$ and THEIA while satisfying existing cosmological, astrophysical, and terrestrial bounds.
papers.summary: The paper proposes that the single LZ nuclear recoil event can be explained by an inelastic dark matter candidate in a gauged U(1)_X hidden sector, whose spontaneous symmetry breaking generates a pseudo-Dirac fermion and a first-order phase transition that produces a stochastic gravitational-wave background. It maps the symmetry-breaking scale to both the direct-detection kinematics and the GW signal, outlining parameter space consistent with relic abundance and future interferometer sensitivities.

papers.title: Linear Response to Black Hole Deformations
papers.abstract: Modifications of gravity beyond (vacuum) General Relativity have a subtle impact on the physics around black holes. Describing these effects across different observables is, however, a priori strongly model dependent. While effective descriptions of the geometry allow to efficiently capture deviations from benchmark predictions, they sometimes lack a clear passage towards (effective) new physics. Inspired by linear response theory, in this work I therefore propose a formalism that allows to calculate leading corrections of observables relative to the Schwarzschild black hole anywhere in space-time (outside of the horizon): the order of corrections is fixed through an eigenvalue $\mathcal{E}$ of the Einstein tensor, which is identified with an external energy momentum tensor that generates the deformation of the geometry. In this ways, $\mathcal{E}$ can be linked to effective physics models. Focusing on spherically symmetric and static black holes, I illustrate the approach at the hand of a number of observables in the vicinity of the horizon, such as characteristic quantities of particles moving around the black hole (e.g. the black hole shadow or the radius of the innermost stable circular orbit) or the spectrum of scalar quasi-normal modes. Reversing the logic, I argue that the knowledge of such observables provides non-trivial constraints on $\mathcal{E}$, which in turn grant insights into the effective physics in the vicinity of the black hole.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a linear response framework that quantifies leading corrections to Schwarzschild black hole observables by treating deviations as eigenvalues of the Einstein tensor, effectively linking them to an external energy‑momentum source. The authors illustrate the method on static, spherically symmetric spacetimes, computing shifts in the shadow, ISCO radius, and scalar quasi‑normal mode spectrum, and argue that observational data can constrain the deformation parameter and inform underlying modified‑gravity models.

papers.title: Plasmon modes in triple-point semimetal, its quadratic cousin, and Hopf semimetal
papers.abstract: We study collective charge excitations in pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals within the random-phase approximation, considering both the linearised model with a flat-band and its quadratic-corrected counterpart. We analyse their density response, Drude weights, screening, plasmon dispersion and damping, particle-hole continua, and Friedel oscillations from the long-wavelength to the arbitrary-momentum regime. The quadratic correction renders the flat-band dispersive and endows it with a Fermi surface, thereby affecting the overall response. Comparisons with Weyl and Hopf semimetals reveal how bandstructure and quantum geometry jointly govern collective charge dynamics. While the Drude weights are determined by the Fermi surface and band-velocities, interband screening, plasmon dispersion, and Friedel oscillations reflect the quantum geometry of the eigenstates.
papers.summary: The paper investigates collective charge excitations in pseudospin‑1 triple‑point semimetals using the random‑phase approximation, analyzing density response, Drude weights, screening, plasmon dispersion, damping, particle‑hole continua, and Friedel oscillations for both linear and quadratic band models. It shows how the quadratic correction turns the flat band dispersive, creating a Fermi surface that alters the response, and compares the results to Weyl and Hopf semimetals to highlight the role of bandstructure and quantum geometry.

papers.title: Okubo algebras and Exceptional Periodicity: tetracode gradings, root-lattice obstructions and Clifford cones
papers.abstract: The Okubo algebra brings together ternary gradings, integral root frames and rank-three geometry. We examine how these structures extend to the complex Exceptional Periodicity algebras. With $N=4(n+1)$, a tetracode character gives eight nonzero homogeneous components of dimension $t_n=8n+3+2^{4n}$. On a tip, a compatible grading has zero component of dimension $8n-5$ and eight nonzero components of dimension $1+2^{4n-3}$. The arithmetic behaves differently: for $n\geq2$, the lattice $D_N^+$ has no full-rank orthogonal frame of unscaled $A_2$ lattices. We exhibit failures of the Jacobi and Jordan identities and determine the derivations and full automorphism group of the ambient algebra above level one. We also give a Clifford-module proof, with the normalization fixed by root products, of the published realization of EP tips as special Vinberg $H$-algebras. This identifies a positive real form and yields explicit formulas for its cone, cubic, Cholesky coordinates and rational dual invariant. The cone is symmetric exactly at $n=1$. Its determinant-one hypersurface belongs to the known $L(8n,1,0)$ series, whose $r$- and $c$-maps give homogeneous scalar manifolds for supergravity theories with eight real supercharges.
papers.summary: The paper develops a graded structure on the Okubo algebra and its extensions to the Exceptional Periodicity algebras, analyzing tetracode gradings, root‑lattice obstructions, and Clifford‑module realizations of Vinberg H‑algebras. It identifies a positive real form whose cone and cubic invariants yield homogeneous scalar manifolds of the L(8n,1,0) series, relevant for supergravity theories with eight real supercharges.

papers.title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
papers.abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $\beta$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.
papers.summary: The paper develops a method to compute long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants by expressing them as functionals of an effective phase shift, with the transition profile captured by parabolic‑cylinder functions. It also connects these results to the high-temperature Gaussian β‑ensemble and shows consistency with generalized hydrodynamics predictions for hard‑rod dynamics.

papers.title: Exact two-loop gravitational tail integrals and their ultraviolet-infrared structure
papers.abstract: Gravitational tail-of-tail corrections arise when radiation scatters twice from the mass-monopole field of its source. In the multipolar effective field theory, one of the two-loop topologies contributing to this process involves genuinely coupled loop momenta, preventing its evaluation through nested one-loop integrations. After tensor reduction, this nonfactorizing structure leads to a particularly challenging family of scalar integrals with unbounded numerator powers as the multipole rank increases. We derive exact closed-form expressions for the entire relevant integer numerator domain, valid in generic dimension and accommodating Feynman, retarded, and advanced prescriptions through consistent analytic continuation. Near $d=3+\epsilon$, we also obtain explicit Laurent expansions through $O(\epsilon)$, retaining the subleading information needed in higher-order radiative calculations. While these expansions determine the dimensional poles, identifying their ultraviolet (UV) or infrared (IR) origin requires a separate analysis of momentum regions. We carry out this analysis throughout the integral domain and apply it directly to the coupled tail-of-tail emission diagram for arbitrary electric and magnetic multipoles. In this way, we independently determine the UV and IR residues, and explicitly verify that the complete infrared pole structure, including both double and simple poles, agrees with the exponentiation of the one-loop gravitational tail. The UV residues, calculated directly from hard-momentum regions, reproduce the established multipole anomalous dimensions when combined with the known contributions of the remaining diagrams.
papers.summary: The paper derives exact closed-form expressions for two-loop gravitational tail integrals, including their UV/IR structure, and verifies consistency with known exponentiation of one-loop tails. It provides explicit Laurent expansions near d=3+ε and identifies UV residues matching multipole anomalous dimensions.

papers.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
papers.abstract: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product K\"ahler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $\psi=Bz$ and $\phi=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes a rank‑four deformed Hermitian–Yang–Mills system on the product of two projective lines, classifying all smooth calibrated solutions in terms of linear maps and stability conditions. It gives explicit criteria for existence, uniqueness, and boundary behaviour of solutions, but does not connect to holography or other high‑energy physics frameworks.
